variants.notes: Abstract only: the specific COL4A1 variant is not named, so the HGVS, variant type, zygosity and glaucoma subtype are unknown. The carrier count is inferred as 1 because 27 variants were found in 28 patients, so one variant may occur in two patients, and it is not stated which. The abstract mentions segregation analysis but gives no inheritance result for this variant. Placeholder record: curator should retrieve the full text to identify the variant.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The study used whole-exome sequencing of 257 Chinese patients with glaucoma (125 POAG, 132 PACG), analysing 43 genes associated with anterior segment dysgenesis, microcornea or microphthalmia. The abstract reports one potentially pathogenic COL4A1 variant but does not specify it. The variant details, the carrier and any segregation data are in the full text, which was not provided.

Abstract only. This is a case report of anesthetic management in a child with Gould syndrome (COL4A1/COL4A2-related disorder). The abstract names no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant and gives no inheritance information. The full text may contain variant details, but they were not available here, so no variant record was created.

Only the title and abstract were available. The abstract describes a single proband: a woman in her late 50s with a left parietal-temporal intracerebral haematoma, contralateral microhaemorrhages, migraine and cognitive involvement. She has a family history of young-onset stroke. The authors report a 'pathogenic COL4A2 mutation' but the abstract does not name the variant: no cDNA change, protein change or transcript is given. No record was created because there is no specific variant to record. Segregation, inheritance and any testing of relatives are also not described. A curator should review the full text to obtain the variant and add this proband (n=1, likely inherited given the family history, but unconfirmed). Phenotypes for that record would be cerebrovascular (ICH) and small_vessel (microhaemorrhages).

variants.phenotype_details: 49-year-old Chinese woman with six episodes of acute ischemic stroke over a 7-year disease course; persistent dysarthria, right-sided hemiparesis and ataxia; MRI showed prior ischemic infarctions in bilateral centrum semiovale, periventricular regions, basal ganglia, thalamus and brainstem; diagnosed with COL4A1/COL4A2-related hereditary cerebral small vessel disease.
evidence_quotes: We report the case of a 49-year-old woman presenting with six confirmed episodes of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) over a 7-year disease course.

Whole-exome sequencing identified a pathogenic 13.4‑Mb duplication at 13q32.2‑q34, encompassing the COL4A1 and COL4A2 loci, consistent with the molecular diagnostic criteria for COL4A1/COL4A2-related hCSVD.
Head MRI revealed prior ischemic infarctions in the bilateral centrum semiovale, periventricular regions, basal ganglia, thalamus, and brainstem.
variants.notes: Copy-number gain (duplication), not a deletion; 'deletion_cnv' used as the closest available CNV category. The duplication spans both COL4A1 and COL4A2 (and many other genes in 13q32.2-q34); recorded once under COL4A1 to avoid duplicating a single variant. Exact genomic coordinates, inheritance and family testing not stated in abstract. n_tested=1 reflects a single-patient case report.

extraction.extraction_notes: Abstract only. Single 13.4-Mb duplication at 13q32.2-q34 encompassing both COL4A1 and COL4A2; one record created (gene field set to COL4A1) though the CNV equally involves COL4A2. Large duplication includes many other genes, so attribution to COL4A1/COL4A2 is the authors' interpretation. Coordinates, parental testing, and family history not available from abstract.

Only the title and abstract were available. This is a case report of a 34-year-old male with recurrent pontine strokes and pons-predominant white matter hyperintensities. The disease progressed despite immunosuppression, and the authors attribute it to PADMAL. The abstract states only that 'a COL4A1 mutation was found'. It does not give a nucleotide or protein change, transcript, location (for example the 3'UTR miR-29 binding site typical of PADMAL), or inheritance. Because no specific variant is named, no VariantEvidence record was created. The full text may contain the variant and should be checked by a curator. Phenotype if a record is later added: cerebrovascular (recurrent pontine strokes) and small_vessel (white matter hyperintensities, PADMAL); 1 proband; inheritance not stated.

Consensus guideline/review (European Academy of Neurology Delphi recommendations) on monogenic cerebral small-vessel diseases including COL4A1/2. Only the title and abstract were available; the abstract reports no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in specific individuals.

We report on two adolescent individuals with ocular anterior segment dysgenesis (Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly) presenting with neuropsychiatric symptoms.

variants.notes: Abstract only; the specific COL4A1 variant (nucleotide/protein change, variant type) is not given in the abstract, so variant_type is set to 'other' as a placeholder. Inheritance not stated. Phenotype attribution to patient 2 is inferred from statements applying to both patients.

His twin brother also had severe leukoaraiosis and multiple subcortical microhemorrhages as well as a congenital cataract and vascular tortuosity in the retina.

variants.notes: Abstract only; the specific variant (nucleotide/protein change and type) is not given in the abstract. Inheritance not stated. Renovascular hypertension and alveolar hemorrhage placed under 'other' (renovascular hypertension could arguably be renal involvement).

In this report we propose that COL4A1 and COL4A2 may be candidate genes for congenital heart disease (CHD) in individuals with a deletion in 13q within the 6Mb critical region for cardiac development proposed by Huang et al., [2012].

The single reported variant is a de novo 2.5 Mb 13q33.3q34 deletion spanning many genes; the authors propose COL4A1/COL4A2 as candidate genes for congenital heart disease. It is entered once per gene for one patient, so do not double-count. Exact breakpoints and gene content were not available in the abstract.

Abstract only. This is a case report of a 6-year-old girl described as 'COL4A1 mutation positive', with drug-resistant epilepsy, cerebral palsy and developmental delay, who underwent a complication-free complete corpus callosotomy. The abstract does not name the specific variant, its inheritance, or imaging findings, so no variant record was created. The full text may give the variant and should be checked by a curator.

Abstract-only input. This is a literature review of monogenic causes and candidate genes for young ischemic stroke. COL4A1 is mentioned only as a disease gene, and no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in specific individuals are reported.

Abstract only. This is a retrospective cohort of 62 preterm infants with PVHI, 17 of whom had an atypical presentation. The abstract states: 'In two infants with an atypical presentation who were tested for this, a mutation in the COL4A1 gene was found (reported previously).' The specific COL4A1 variants are not named, and these two infants were reported in an earlier publication, so no variant-level record could be created. The number of infants tested for COL4A1 is not stated. The other variants mentioned are thrombophilia variants in other genes: factor V Leiden G1691A, prothrombin G20210A, and the MTHFR C677T/A1298C polymorphisms. These are not relevant to COL4A1/COL4A2. The full text may name the COL4A1 variants and cite the prior report; a curator should check it and link these two infants to the earlier COL4A1 PVHI/porencephaly report.

Systematic review of published COL4A1 mutation carriers (52 carriers drawn from the literature, 1966 to January 2010). Only the title and abstract were available. The abstract names no specific variants and reports no new individuals; it gives only aggregate phenotype frequencies (stroke 17.3%, leukoaraiosis 63.5%, microbleeds 52.9%, eye 47.6%, kidney 15.4%, muscle 15.4%). Any variant-level data in the full text would come from previously published cases, so no records were created.

Abstract only. This is a French-language review/discussion paper in Bull Acad Natl Med describing three HANAC families with glycine mutations in COL4A1 exons 24 and 25. No specific variants are named in the abstract. These families are likely the same as those reported by Plaisier et al. 2007 (NEJM). No variant records were created because no specific variant designations are given.

Abstract only. The paper reports three closely located COL4A1 glycine mutations in exons 24 and 25, one per family, in three autosomal dominant HANAC families. These were identified by linkage at the COL4A1-COL4A2 locus followed by sequencing of COL4A1 cDNA from skin fibroblasts. The abstract does not give the specific variant nomenclature (no c. or p. designations). It also does not give which exon each variant lies in, the number of affected carriers per family, or segregation details. No variant records were created because the variants cannot be identified from the provided text. Reported phenotypes across the families: hematuria and bilateral large renal cysts (renal_hanac), intracranial aneurysms and a systemic angiopathy affecting small vessels and large arteries (cerebrovascular/small_vessel), and muscle cramps (muscle). The abstract also reports complex basement-membrane defects in kidney and skin on histology. The full text is needed to extract the three variants, carrier counts and inheritance, and each should be recorded as missense_glycine.

Abstract only. This is a computational RNA-seq somatic mutation profiling study in small-cell lung cancer. COL4A1 is named only as an implicated oncogene. No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variant is reported in a specific individual. The 'G > A' and 'C > T' strings flagged by PubTator refer to genome-wide mutational signature transitions, not COL4A1 variants. The variants are somatic tumour mutations, not germline variants relevant to COL4A1/COL4A2-related disease.

Abstract only. This is an association study of 300 Caucasian Fabry disease patients, stratified by eGFR and studied with whole-exome sequencing. The only COL4A2 variant mentioned is rs7320419, an upstream non-coding variant. It was reported as associated with an odds ratio below one, a potential protective effect against nephropathy progression, with FDR < 0.05. This is an association SNP and not a candidate causal variant in specific affected individuals, so no variant record was created. No COL4A1 variants were reported.

variants.phenotype_details: 7-year-old female with epilepsy; diagnosed with Brain small vessel disease 1 with ocular anomalies (specific imaging and ocular findings not described in abstract).

Sanger sequencing confirmed that her parents both had the wild-type genotype for this variant.
The child was a 7-year-old female with a diagnosis of epilepsy.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Conclusion writes the variant as c.1792T>C (p.G598S), inconsistent with c.1792G>A in Results; c.1792G>A taken as correct given Gly>Ser. Transcript not stated. Only epilepsy is explicitly reported; small-vessel and ocular features are implied by the diagnosis label but not described, so only 'other' is listed. Paternity confirmation not mentioned, but both parents tested wild-type.

extraction.extraction_notes: Title and abstract only. Single proband with a de novo COL4A1 glycine substitution. Specific neuroimaging and ocular findings are not detailed in the abstract. There is a c. nomenclature inconsistency between Results (c.1792G>A) and Conclusion (c.1792T>C).

variants.phenotype_details: Recurrent ischemic strokes since age 32; brain MRI showed multiple acute and chronic lacunar infarcts in the pons and bilateral cerebral hemispheres; diagnosed as PADMAL.

Identity testing confirmed the biological parentage, classifying the c.*32G > T variant as a de novo mutation.
The patient experienced recurrent ischemic strokes since age 32.
Brain MRI showed multiple acute and chronic lacunar infarcts in the pons and bilateral cerebral hemispheres.
variants.notes: Abstract only. 3'UTR variant in miR-29-binding site; transcript not stated. The variant itself was previously reported in other PADMAL families, but this proband is new. Parentage confirmed by identity/haplotype testing, so de novo is confirmed.

Abstract only. This is a case-control association study of the intronic COL4A2 indel polymorphism rs34802628 (4-bp ins/del), comparing 497 stomach adenocarcinoma patients with 804 healthy controls using odds ratios and p-values. It is a common polymorphism studied for association, not a candidate causal variant in specific affected individuals, so no variant record was created. The study also includes expression analyses from GEPIA, TCGA and RT-PCR.

Abstract only. This is a case-control association study of the COL4A1 polymorphism rs605143 (G/A), genotyped by PCR-RFLP in 386 subjects (120 T2DM, 120 diabetic nephropathy, 146 healthy controls). Results are reported as genotype and allele odds ratios (AA genotype 5.87- and 8.01-fold risk; A allele 2.29- and 2.81-fold risk). These are association-SNP results, not variants reported in specific affected individuals as a candidate cause of disease. Under the extraction rules, no variant records were created.

Genetic testing revealed a novel variant, c.2321G>A:p.(Gly774Glu), in COL4A2.

One family (mother and daughter); the abstract does not state which individual is the proband or explicitly confirm carrier status in both, though it implies both carry the variant. The mother is likely the proband, but whether she inherited the variant is unknown, so inheritance is recorded as unknown. Total carriers are left null because they are not explicitly stated. Transcript not stated.

variants.phenotype_details: Visceral artery aneurysms (VAAs) in seven affected family members; the variant was absent in one relative with a visceral artery pseudoaneurysm. Age at onset not stated in the abstract.

evidence_quotes: Here, we present a striking family with seven individuals affected by VAAs, and one individual affected by a visceral artery pseudoaneurysm.
Two of seven top-ranking variants, NC_000013.11:g.108154659C>T and NC_000013.11:g.110409638C>T, were found in all VAA-affected individuals, but not in the individual affected by the pseudoaneurysm.
The second variant is in a candidate cis-regulatory element in the fourth intron of COL4A2, proximal to COL4A1.
variants.notes: Abstract only. This is a genomic (NC_000013.11) non-coding variant in intron 4 of COL4A2 and lies in a candidate cis-regulatory element. It was prioritised by DeepSEA ranking combined with linkage analysis. It segregates with VAA in one large pedigree, with 7 affected carriers. The abstract says the proband's parents were exome sequenced, but it does not state which parent carries the variant, so inheritance is recorded as unknown. The phenotype (visceral artery aneurysm) does not fit the standard COL4A1/2 categories and is recorded as 'other'. PubTator associates rs188744081 with this variant; that rsID is not in the paper text. The paper does not give the total number of family members sequenced, so n_tested is 0.

extraction.extraction_notes: Title and abstract only. A second co-segregating variant, NC_000013.11:g.108154659C>T, is not described as lying in COL4A1/COL4A2. Its position (about 108.15 Mb on chr13) is well outside the COL4A1/COL4A2 locus (about 110.1-110.4 Mb), so it was not extracted, despite PubTator tagging it to COL4A2. The causal role of the COL4A2 intronic variant is proposed as a candidate only; no functional validation is described in the abstract.

variants.phenotype_details: Peters anomaly type I in a baby girl; no other systemic features described in the abstract.

Ophthalmologic examination led to the diagnosis of PA type I in the baby girl.

Whole exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing identified the de novo mutation c.181_189delinsAGGTTTCCG; p.Gly61Arg in the COL4A1 gene in the child, whereas no other putatively causative variants in established genes associated with anterior segment dysgenesis were present.

The nucleotide change is a 9-bp delins that, per the authors, results in a single glycine substitution (p.Gly61Arg); classified as missense_glycine based on protein consequence, could alternatively be considered an in-frame delins. Transcript not stated. De novo status counted as confirmed because both biological parents were sequenced; parentage confirmation method not described in abstract. p.Gly61 lies in the N-terminal region (7S domain region), not the triple-helical Gly-X-Y domain, which a curator may wish to note.

variants.phenotype_details: Adult man with recurrent cerebral infarcts; MRI showed multiple lacunar infarcts, numerous deep and lobar microhemorrhages, and advanced leukoaraiosis. Age at onset not stated in abstract.

variants.phenotype_details: 17-year-old boy with recurrent intracranial hemorrhages in periventricular white matter (late onset, after 10 years of age); childhood cerebral palsy with intracranial calcifications, developmental delay, epilepsy; leukoencephalopathy; severe persistent motor and cognitive deficits.

He had been followed-up as a child with cerebral palsy bearing intracranial calcifications, developmental delay and epilepsy.
The whole-exome sequencing revealed that he carried a de novo mutation in COL4A1 (p.Gly696Ser).

Abstract only. The paper is an association study of the common COL4A1 polymorphism rs3783107 (G>A) in a Finnish cohort of 771 people (331 hypertensive cases and 440 normotensive controls). It reports odds ratios and p-values for associations with hypertension, asthma and eczema, and finds no association with cerebrovascular events. No candidate causal variants are reported in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created, per the instructions on association SNPs.

variants.phenotype_details: PADMAL (pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy) with MRI lesions in the pons, white matter and cervical spinal cord; skin biopsy showed thickened basal lamina in vessels. Ages at onset not stated in abstract. One healthy family member also carried the variant.
evidence_quotes: We identified a mutation located at the binding site of miR-29 (microRNA-29) in 3' untranslated region of COL4A1(c.*32G>A).
The pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy patients in this pedigree carried this variant, whereas other healthy family members but one did not.
Magnetic resonance imaging showed lesions in the pons, white matter, and cervical spinal cord.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Single Chinese pedigree with multiple affected members; the number of affected carriers is not stated. Inheritance is autosomal dominant within the pedigree, but the abstract does not specify which parent the proband inherited the variant from, so it is counted as unknown. One unaffected family member carried the variant, which suggests incomplete penetrance or presymptomatic status. Spinal cord involvement is recorded under 'other'.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. Carrier counts, ages at onset and transcript are not given. No functional assays of the miR-29 binding site are described in the abstract.

Abstract only. This is a case-control association study of seven common COL4A2 SNPs (rs3803230, rs391859, rs4103, rs445348, rs76425569, rs7990383, rs9515185). The study included 406 lacunar stroke patients and 425 controls from a Xinjiang Han population. Results are reported only as genotype and haplotype odds ratios and p-values. No variants are reported in specific individuals as a candidate cause of disease, so no variant records were created, per the rule excluding association SNPs.

variants.phenotype_details: Schizencephaly (mainly asymmetrical) with porencephaly or ventriculomegaly; no microbleeds, microcalcifications, neuromuscular or hematological anomalies.
evidence_quotes: One de novo missense COL4A1 mutation (c.3715 G > A, p.(Gly1239Arg)) and two COL4A2 mutations were found, respectively in one familial case (c.4129G > A, p.(Gly1377Arg)) and one sporadic patient (c.1776+1G > A).
We screened for COL4A1/A2 mutations in 9 patients with schizencephaly and/or polymicrogyria suspected to be caused by vascular disruption and leading to a cerebral haemorrhagic ischaemic event.
Brain malformations included a combination of schizencephaly, mainly asymmetrical, with porencephaly or ventriculomegaly (3/3 mutated patients).
variants.notes: Abstract only; called de novo but parental testing not described in abstract. Transcript not stated.

variants.phenotype_details: Schizencephaly (mainly asymmetrical) with porencephaly or ventriculomegaly in proband; familial case.
evidence_quotes: One de novo missense COL4A1 mutation (c.3715 G > A, p.(Gly1239Arg)) and two COL4A2 mutations were found, respectively in one familial case (c.4129G > A, p.(Gly1377Arg)) and one sporadic patient (c.1776+1G > A).
Brain malformations included a combination of schizencephaly, mainly asymmetrical, with porencephaly or ventriculomegaly (3/3 mutated patients).
variants.notes: Abstract only. Described as 'familial case', suggesting inheritance, but carrier parent not explicitly stated, so inheritance recorded as unknown; number of carrier relatives not given.

variants.phenotype_details: Schizencephaly (mainly asymmetrical) with porencephaly or ventriculomegaly; sporadic patient.
evidence_quotes: One de novo missense COL4A1 mutation (c.3715 G > A, p.(Gly1239Arg)) and two COL4A2 mutations were found, respectively in one familial case (c.4129G > A, p.(Gly1377Arg)) and one sporadic patient (c.1776+1G > A).
Brain malformations included a combination of schizencephaly, mainly asymmetrical, with porencephaly or ventriculomegaly (3/3 mutated patients).
variants.notes: Abstract only. 'Sporadic' does not indicate parental testing; inheritance recorded as unknown.

extraction.extraction_notes: Abstract only. Cohort of 9 patients with schizencephaly and/or polymicrogyria. Three additional COL4A1 variants of unknown significance in three other cases are mentioned but not specified in the abstract, so no records were created for them. Transcripts not stated.

Abstract only. This is a case-control association study of six common COL4A1 SNPs (including rs1961495 and rs1411040) genotyped in 351 cerebral palsy patients and 220 healthy controls from a Chinese Han population. Results are reported as allele p-values and odds ratios. No specific variants are reported in specific individuals as a candidate cause of disease, so no variant records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Autosomal dominant disorder in a three-generation family comprising porencephaly, focal epilepsy, and lens opacities (cataracts). Ages at onset not stated in abstract.
variants.reported_classification: predicted to be damaging by multiple bioinformatics tools
evidence_quotes: We describe a family with an autosomal dominant disorder comprising porencephaly, focal epilepsy, and lens opacities, which was negative for mutations in COL4A1.
Using whole exome sequencing of three affected individuals from three generations, we identified a rare variant in COL4A2.

This COL4A2 (c.2399G>A, p.G800E, CCDS41907.1) variant was predicted to be damaging by multiple bioinformatics tools and affects an invariable glycine residue that is essential for the formation of collagen IV heterotrimers.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Single family; inheritance coded as inherited based on autosomal dominant transmission across three generations, but carrier status of proband's parent is not explicitly described in the abstract. Three affected individuals underwent exome sequencing; total carrier count and segregation details not stated. Total cohort/denominator not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. Segregation, number of carriers, detailed clinical findings and ages at onset would be in the full text.

Abstract only. This is a case-control GWAS replication study of cervical dystonia (252 cases, 342 controls, Spanish population). The only COL4A1-related variant is the common association SNP rs619152 in the COL4A1 region. It was excluded because of assay failure, and it is an association polymorphism, not a variant in specific affected individuals. No COL4A1/COL4A2 variant-level data were reported, so no records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Autosomal dominant familial retinal arteriolar tortuosity (FRAT) in three affected family members; no cerebral, neurologic, renal, cardiac or vascular anomalies recognized. Age at onset not stated in abstract.
evidence_quotes: Our aim was to determine the molecular cause of autosomal dominant familial retinal arteriolar tortuosity (FRAT) in a family with three affected subjects.
Sanger sequencing confirmed that all three patients harbored the same pathogenetic mutation in COL4A1.
The p. Gly510Arg variant in COL4A1 was absent in DNA from an available unaffected daughter, from a set of control alleles, and from publicly available databases.
No cerebral, neurologic, renal, cardiac or vascular anomalies were recognized in the pedigree described here.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Single family with three affected carriers; dominant segregation implied, but which affected member is the proband and parental carrier status are not specified, so inheritance recorded as unknown. The same variant was previously reported in an unrelated HANAC family (different family); this FRAT family appears to be newly reported. Transcript not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. Pedigree structure, ages and transcript not available.

Abstract only. This is a case-control association study of 40 polymorphisms in 31 candidate genes in 3433 unrelated Japanese individuals (1328 with myocardial infarction, 2105 controls). The only COL4A1 variant is the common polymorphism rs3742207 (A>C, Gln1334His), which is reported as associated with MI risk. Per the instructions, no record was created for this association SNP. No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific affected individuals as a candidate cause of disease.

variants.phenotype_details: Second-trimester fetal intracranial hemorrhage: prenatal ultrasound showed a mass in the fetal left intracranial cavity; repeated MRI showed an evolving mass in the left frontal parietal lobe. Karyotype, CMA and amniotic fluid CMV PCR were negative. Pregnancy terminated; no fetal pathology.
evidence_quotes: However, the whole exome sequencing (WES) identified a heterozygous missense mutation that was considered pathogenic in the COL4A1 (NM_001844.6) gene: c.3715G > A (p.Gly1239Arg).
Repeated subsequent MRI detected an evolving mass in the left frontal parietal lobe.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Parental testing and inheritance are not described in the abstract. Hemorrhage is inferred from the title (fetal intracranial hemorrhage). The NM_001844.6 transcript is as stated by the authors.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. Inheritance (de novo vs inherited) is not reported in the abstract; the full text may contain parental testing results.

variants.phenotype_details: Six affected individuals (43-72 years) from a single two-generation HANAC family; DNA sequencing done only in the proband. Four had arterial hypertension, three had kidney dysfunction (one on dialysis), five had retinal arteriolar tortuosity with arteriolar loops; reduced wall-to-lumen ratio, arteriolar irregularities in the two oldest, and increased flicker-induced vasodilation in three.
evidence_quotes: Clinical data from six affected individuals (43 to 72 years old) from a single family comprising two generations were collected.
DNA sequencing was done in the proband.

DNA sequencing of the proband revealed a heterozygous deletion of COL4A1 (NM_001845) at position 1120 in the intron 20 resulting in the loss of splicing donor site for exon 20 (c.1120 + 2_1120 + 8del heterozygote).
Four patients had arterial hypertension, and three had kidney dysfunction, one of which under dialysis.
By fundus examination, five had typical retinal arteriolar tortuosity with arteriolar loops.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Only the proband was genotyped; the segregation status of the other 5 affected relatives is not stated in the abstract, so n_total_carriers is left null. Inheritance in the proband is not explicitly described, although the family is two-generation and has multiple affected members. Hypertension is listed under 'other'. The splice effect is inferred by the authors; no functional assay is described.

extraction.extraction_notes: Title and abstract only. The abstract text is truncated in the flicker results section.

variants.phenotype_details: Female; fetal porencephaly; severe neonatal hemolytic anemia; drug-resistant epilepsy, global developmental delay, spastic quadriplegia in childhood; progressive white matter atrophy from gestation to 5-year follow-up or later.
evidence_quotes: Their mutations were c.4843G>A (p.Glu1615Lys), c.1835G>A (p.Gly612Asp), and c.3556+1G>T respectively.

All the three cases represented porencephaly in the fetal period; severe hemolytic anemia in the neonatal period; and drug-resistant epilepsy, global developmental delay, and spastic quadriplegia in their childhood.
variants.notes: Abstract only; inheritance not stated. Progressive white matter atrophy reported for all three; classed as small_vessel cautiously (atrophy rather than leukoencephalopathy per se). Unclear which patient had minor cerebral hemorrhage.

variants.phenotype_details: Female; fetal porencephaly; severe neonatal hemolytic anemia; drug-resistant epilepsy, global developmental delay, spastic quadriplegia in childhood; progressive white matter atrophy from gestation to 5-year follow-up or later.
evidence_quotes: Their mutations were c.4843G>A (p.Glu1615Lys), c.1835G>A (p.Gly612Asp), and c.3556+1G>T respectively.

All the three cases represented porencephaly in the fetal period; severe hemolytic anemia in the neonatal period; and drug-resistant epilepsy, global developmental delay, and spastic quadriplegia in their childhood.
variants.notes: Abstract only; inheritance not stated.

variants.phenotype_details: Female; fetal porencephaly; severe neonatal hemolytic anemia; drug-resistant epilepsy, global developmental delay, spastic quadriplegia in childhood; progressive white matter atrophy from gestation to 5-year follow-up or later.
evidence_quotes: Their mutations were c.4843G>A (p.Glu1615Lys), c.1835G>A (p.Gly612Asp), and c.3556+1G>T respectively.
Brain MRI and CT showed progressive white matter atrophy from gestation to five-year follow-up or later.
variants.notes: Abstract only; inheritance not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Abstract only. Three unrelated female patients each with a distinct COL4A1 variant; transcript, inheritance and cohort denominator not given. Minor asymptomatic cerebral hemorrhage occurred in one unspecified patient. Possible overlap with prior reports cannot be assessed from abstract.

variants.as_written: c.2972G>A, causing the aminoacidic substitution Gly991Glu
variants.phenotype_details: Mother (65 y): hematuria, adult-onset seizures, closed lip schizencephaly of right lateral sulcus with surrounding polymicrogyria and subcortical heterotopia. Son (40 y): post-term birth with neonatal distress, psychomotor developmental delay, congenital left leg paresis, strabismus, childhood-onset focal motor seizures; MRI right nucleus-capsular porencephalic cavitation with ipsilateral ventricular enlargement, focal right occipital cortico-subcortical encephalomalacia, small left frontal subcortical heterotopic band.
evidence_quotes: The first patient is a 65-year-old woman with hematuria and adult-onset seizures.
The second patient is a 40-year-old man, her son.
Brain MRI showed a right nucleus-capsular porencephalic cavitation with enlargement of the homolateral ventricle and a focal right occipital cortico-subcortical encephalomalacia.
We tested both patients with a NGS panel for genetic epilepsies, which evidenced a missense mutation in COL4A2 gene (c.2972G>A, causing the aminoacidic substitution Gly991Glu).
variants.notes: Abstract only. One family (mother and son), both carriers; counted as one proband. Inheritance coded as inherited assuming the son inherited from his carrier mother; the mother's own inheritance is not stated. Strabismus was listed under ocular; it is not among the listed ocular examples, so a curator may prefer to classify it as other. Transcript not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The proband designation and the direction of inheritance (mother to son) are inferred from the description of the family. n_tested=2 reflects the two family members who were sequenced.

Abstract only. This is a case-control association study (410 cases, 386 controls) of 13 mirSNPs in clopidogrel-metabolism genes and cardiovascular disease risk. The only COL4A1 variant is the common polymorphism rs874204, reported as associated with CVDs. Because this is an association SNP and not a candidate causal variant in specific affected individuals, no variant record was created.

variants.phenotype_details: Singleton fetus at 25 weeks gestation: mild ventriculomegaly, patchy ischemic infarction, extensive subacute and chronic hemorrhage not respecting vascular territories, encephaloclastic cysts, closed lip schizencephaly on fetal MRI; fetal echocardiogram showed cardiomegaly, right ventricular hypertrophy and tricuspid insufficiency; cataract detected postnatally.
evidence_quotes: A singleton fetus was referred to fetal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 25 weeks due to mild ventriculomegaly and an abnormal fetal echocardiogram showing cardiomegaly, right ventricular hypertrophy and tricuspid insufficiency.
Patchy areas of ischemic infarction, extensive subacute and chronic hemorrhage not respecting vascular territories, encephaloclastic cysts and closed lip schizencephaly were identified.
Cataract was detected postnatally.
The anomalies were caused by a pathogenic mutation (c.353 G>A; p.G118D) in the COL4A1 gene.
variants.notes: Abstract only; transcript not stated; inheritance not reported in abstract. Described as novel mutation. Protein HGVS expanded from p.G118D.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available; inheritance, transcript and family details may be in full text.

variants.phenotype_details: 17-year-old boy with right hemispheric epilepsy treated by functional hemispherectomy; on postoperative day 8 developed diffuse cerebral vasospasm and delayed cerebral ischemia with bilateral restricted diffusion and minimal residual postoperative subarachnoid hemorrhage; died.
variants.reported_classification: autosomal dominant heterozygous COL4A1 gene mutation
evidence_quotes: A 17-year-old boy presented with right hemispheric epilepsy and a previously diagnosed autosomal dominant heterozygous COL4A1 gene mutation (c.4380T>G;p.Cys1460Trp).
Magnetic resonance imaging revealed areas of restricted diffusion throughout bilateral hemispheres that was explained by severe vasospasm and minimal cerebral blood flow seen on cerebral angiography.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Transcript not stated. The term 'autosomal dominant' describes the inheritance mode, not a tested carrier parent, so inheritance is recorded as unknown. The variant was 'previously diagnosed', so this patient may already have been reported elsewhere, but no prior report is cited. The underlying cause of the epilepsy (for example porencephaly) is not described in the abstract.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The full text may contain details on imaging, family history and inheritance that are not captured here.

variants.phenotype_details: 2-year-old boy with porencephaly; recurrent rhabdomyolysis triggered by viral or bacterial infections; obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy requiring surgical intervention; skeletal muscle biopsy compatible with fiber-type disproportion; ultrastructure showed collagen disarray, reduced electron density of basement membrane of capillary endothelial cells and muscle fibers, and dilated endoplasmic reticulum in capillary endothelial cells.
variants.functional_evidence: Patient muscle biopsy electron microscopy showed collagen disarray, reduced basement membrane electron density, and dilated endoplasmic reticulum in capillary endothelial cells.
evidence_quotes: We report the case of a 2-year-old boy with porencephaly, who harbored a de novo COL4A1 mutation of c.1853G > A, p. (Gly618Glu) and exhibited recurrent rhabdomyolysis with viral or bacterial infections.
Moreover, he developed obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy which required surgical intervention.
Skeletal muscle biopsy revealed findings compatible with fiber-type disproportion.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Called de novo, but parental testing is not described in the abstract, so it is recorded as assumed de novo. Transcript not stated. No author classification was given beyond 'mutation'.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. Details of parental testing, the transcript, and any additional examinations may be in the full text.

Abstract only. This is an association study of 6 COL4A1 SNPs, including rs532625, measured against hypertensive ICH outcome (disability and death) in 181 Chinese Han patients. These are common polymorphisms analysed by genotype and allele association, not candidate causal variants in specific individuals, so no variant records were created.

Abstract only. This is a mouse functional study of the COL4A1 p.G498V mutation (mice expressing the disease-causing mutation), which describes cerebral micro- and macrohaemorrhages and retinal arterial smooth muscle cell loss. The abstract reports no new human patients carrying COL4A1/COL4A2 variants, so no variant records were created. Functional findings for p.G498V in mice: transient blood-brain barrier permeability with early microhaemorrhages, and progressive apoptosis-mediated smooth muscle cell degeneration in deep brain and retinal arteries, which correlated with macrohaemorrhage burden.

Abstract only. This is a case-control association study (181 hypertensive ICH patients vs 197 hypertensive controls, Chinese Han) of 6 common COL4A1 SNPs (e.g. rs3742207, rs11069830, rs679505, rs544012) genotyped by MassARRAY. The SNPs are reported with allele, genotype and haplotype associations, not as candidate causal variants in specific individuals. Per the extraction rules, no variant records were created.

Abstract-only meta-analysis of collagen gene SNP associations with intracranial aneurysm (14 studies, 13,709 patients). The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are common polymorphisms analysed for association (e.g., COL4A1 rs3783107, reported with odds ratios and p-values; 6 COL4A1 SNPs and 1 COL4A2 SNP in total). No specific variants are reported in specific affected individuals, so no records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Italian family; variant segregated in four subjects with variable neurological phenotypes: leukoencephalopathy with muscle symptoms, brain small-vessel disease, and mild infantile encephalopathy; one carrier had no neurological symptoms but an MRI with a specific white matter anomaly. Ages at onset not given in abstract.
variants.reported_classification: novel mutation; predicted as being deleterious by bioinformatics tools
evidence_quotes: We studied two Italian families in which the proband had a clinical diagnosis of COL4A1-related disorder.

The c.1249G>C (p.Gly417Arg) segregated in four subjects with variable neurological phenotypes, namely leukoencephalopathy with muscle symptoms, brain small-vessel disease, and mild infantile encephalopathy.
A fourth case was a carrier of the mutation without any neurological symptoms and an MRI with a specific white matter anomaly.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Segregation in family implies familial transmission, but the abstract does not state which parent of the proband carries it, so proband inheritance recorded as unknown. Total of 4 carriers inferred from 'segregated in four subjects'; abstract wording ('A fourth case') is slightly ambiguous whether the asymptomatic carrier is among the four. Transcript not stated.

variants.phenotype_details: Proband (female): temporary motor impairment at age 14, mild imbalance at age 30 during third trimester of twin pregnancy; anomaly of the left brain hemisphere documented prenatally in one fetus. Both male dizygotic twins (carriers) had severe motor delay, early convulsions, and leukoencephalopathy.
variants.reported_classification: novel mutation; predicted as being deleterious by bioinformatics tools
evidence_quotes: The c.2662G>C (p.Gly888Arg) mutation was de novo in the proband.

After a temporary motor impairment at age 14, the subject complained of mild imbalance at age 30, during the third trimester of her twin pregnancy, when an anomaly of the left brain hemisphere was documented in one fetus.
Both her male dizygotic twins presented a severe motor delay, early convulsions, and leukoencephalopathy, and were carriers of the mutation.
variants.notes: Abstract only; de novo status stated but parental testing/parentage confirmation not described in abstract, so recorded as assumed. Proband plus two carrier twins = 3 carriers. Nature of fetal left hemisphere anomaly not specified (placed under 'other').

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. Two Italian families each with one proband; n_tested set to 0 because no screened cohort denominator is given. Transcript and full family details (pedigrees, MRI) not available.

variants.phenotype_details: Daughter (proband; title refers to fetus): porencephaly and an episode of microangiopathic hemolysis in infancy. Father: HANAC (adult-onset hemorrhagic stroke with cerebral aneurysm, retinal arterial tortuosity, renal cysts, thenar muscle cramp, per the abstract's definition of HANAC).
evidence_quotes: We report on a girl with porencephaly and an episode of microangiopathic hemolysis in infancy and her father with HANAC, both of whom had a heterozygous missense mutation of COL4A1 (c.3715G>A, p.G1239R).
The current observation implies phenotypic diversities of COL4A1 mutations.
variants.notes: Abstract only. The girl is treated as the proband, with the variant inherited from her affected father. The specific HANAC features in the father are inferred from the abstract's general definition of HANAC and may not all be present. The transcript was not stated. The 'other' system was assigned for microangiopathic hemolysis.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The detailed phenotypes, any prior report of this family, the transcript and any functional data could not be checked against the full text.

variants.as_written: G2159A transition (c.2159G>A) that leads to the missense mutation p.Gly720Asp
variants.phenotype_details: Ocular phenotype of variable severity observed in all affected relatives; anterior segment dysgenesis reminiscent of Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly (described collectively for the paper).
evidence_quotes: The G2159A transition (c.2159G>A) that leads to the missense mutation p.Gly720Asp was identified in family A.
An ocular phenotype of variable severity was observed in all affected relatives.
We clinically evaluated 7 patients from 2 unrelated families in whom ocular features segregated with COL4A1 mutations that were identified by direct sequencing.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Number of carriers in family A not stated (7 patients across both families). Ocular features segregated with the variant in the family, implying familial transmission, but the proband's parental carrier status is not explicitly stated, so inheritance recorded as unknown. Cerebrovascular disorders are mentioned only generally in the conclusions and not attributed to specific carriers. Possible overlap with prior reports of this family cannot be assessed from the abstract.

variants.phenotype_details: One patient from family B displayed notable ocular features (anterior segment dysgenesis type anomalies reminiscent of Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly, described collectively).
evidence_quotes: The missense mutation c.2263G>A, p.Gly755Arg was identified in family B.
One patient from family B also displayed notable ocular features.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Number of carriers in family B and inheritance not stated. Cerebrovascular involvement is not specifically attributed to this family in the abstract. Possible overlap with earlier reports of this family cannot be assessed from the abstract.

extraction.extraction_notes: Title and abstract only. 7 patients from 2 unrelated families were clinically evaluated; per-family carrier counts, the sequencing denominator, and detailed phenotypes (including any cerebrovascular findings) are not available. Families may have been reported previously (e.g., in earlier COL4A1 cerebrovascular reports), but this cannot be verified from the abstract.

Review article (abstract only). The variants G562E, G749S, G805R, G1130D, G1236R, G1423R, G720D, G1580R and G755R are listed as previously reported COL4A1 stroke syndrome mutations; no new individuals are reported, so no variant records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Index case (14-year-old boy): stroke at age 14 and again 6 months later; diffuse leukoencephalopathy with microhaemorrhages on MRI; cataracts. Carrier mother: long-standing episodic headaches diagnosed as migraine; leukoencephalopathy with microhaemorrhages; cataracts. Untested grandmother (died age 73): recurrent strokes at 18 and 49 years, initially diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, leukoencephalopathy with microhaemorrhages, cataracts. No porencephaly; no retinal arterial changes.
evidence_quotes: We describe a three generation family with recurrent strokes and cataracts.
The index case, a 14 year old boy presented with stroke at the age of 14 years and again 6 months later.
MRI scanning showed a diffuse leukoencephalopathy with microhaemorrhages in all three individuals.
Sequence analysis of COL4A1 revealed the heterozygous missense mutation c.2263G-->A in exon 30, responsible for a glycine-to-arginine substitution (p.Gly755Arg) in both the index case and mother.
Grandmother died at the age of 73 years and DNA analysis was not possible.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Two genotyped carriers (index case and mother); the affected grandmother was not tested. No transcript stated. Migraine in the mother is placed under 'other'.

extraction.extraction_notes: Abstract only; full text not available. Single three-generation family. Exon 30 location stated; no reference transcript given.

variants.phenotype_details: Two preterm siblings with antenatal-onset intracerebral (parenchymal) hemorrhage and established porencephaly present at birth; asymptomatic at birth; diagnosed by cranial ultrasound and confirmed by MRI. Mild antenatal trauma in the first infant only. Affected mother and maternal grandfather had leukoencephalopathy; their carrier status is not stated in the abstract.
evidence_quotes: Both infants had a novel G1580R mutation in the COL4A1 gene, encoding procollagen type IV alpha1.
Mutation analysis of the COL4A1 gene was performed in the infants and in their mother.

Two preterm infants with antenatal intracerebral hemorrhage and established porencephaly, as well as their affected mother and grandfather, underwent neurological and ophthalmological examination and magnetic resonance imaging of the brain.
Leukoencephalopathy was present in the mother and in her father.
variants.notes: Abstract only. The two affected siblings were counted as one family and one proband. The mother was tested and described as affected (leukoencephalopathy), so maternal inheritance is likely. However, the abstract does not state her genotype, so inheritance is recorded as unknown, and small_vessel is not listed because carrier status of the affected mother/grandfather is unconfirmed. n_tested=3 (two infants plus mother). The c. notation and transcript are not given.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The full text may state the mother's genotype (likely carrier) and the grandfather's testing status, which would change the inheritance counts to inherited and add small_vessel to the phenotype systems.

variants.phenotype_details: 25-year-old normotensive male with history of infantile hemiparesis; recurrent spontaneous deep intracerebral hemorrhages since age 17, occurring during sports activities; severely disabled. MRI: ventricular enlargement, diffuse white-matter abnormalities, newly appearing deep silent microbleeds. No family history of stroke or infantile hemiparesis.
evidence_quotes: We performed a clinical and genetic study of a 25-year-old-patient with an 8-year history of recurrent ICHs.
This young, normotensive patient with a history of infantile hemiparesis had experienced, since the age of 17, recurrent, spontaneous, deep ICHs occurring during sports activities.
Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed ventricular enlargement, diffuse white-matter abnormalities, and newly appearing, deep, silent microbleeds.
There was no family history of stroke or infantile hemiparesis.
A novel COL4A1 mutation (G805R) was identified.
variants.notes: Abstract only. The case is described as sporadic with no family history, but the abstract does not describe parental testing, so inheritance is recorded as unknown rather than de novo. Protein numbering is given without a reference transcript; no c. notation is given in the abstract.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The full text may contain parental testing results, cDNA notation and segregation data that are not captured here.

low_confidence: candidate CNVs across NOTCH3, LMNB1, and COL4A2

variants.as_written: candidate CNVs across NOTCH3, LMNB1, and COL4A2
variants.phenotype_details: Patient(s) suspected of familial cerebral small vessel disease who had previously tested negative for SNVs/indels in NOTCH3, HTRA1, COL4A1, COL4A2, TREX1, GLA and FOXC1; no individual phenotype details or ages given in the abstract.
variants.reported_classification: candidate CNV; potential cause of CSVD
evidence_quotes: In this study we performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) on 111 patients suspected of familial CSVD that had previously tested negative for pathogenic variants in seven known CSVD genes (NOTCH3, HTRA1, COL4A1, COL4A2, TREX1, GLA, and FOXC1).

This work identified four candidate CNVs across NOTCH3, LMNB1, and COL4A2 which are potential causes of CSVD and highlights the need for further investigation of more complex forms of genetic variation and their potential roles as causal of CSVD.
variants.notes: Abstract only. The COL4A2 CNV is not specified (type, i.e. deletion vs duplication, size, breakpoints, and the number of COL4A2 CNVs among the four are not stated); n_probands=1 is a minimum inferred from the abstract. variant_type deletion_cnv is used as the generic CNV category, not a confirmed deletion. Inheritance and segregation are not described. The phenotype is the cohort-level inclusion criterion (suspected familial CSVD), not an individual description.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The abstract reports four candidate CNVs across NOTCH3, LMNB1 and COL4A2 among 111 WES-screened patients with suspected familial CSVD, but does not specify the COL4A2 CNV(s), the carriers, or their phenotypes. A single placeholder low-confidence COL4A2 CNV record was created; the curator should consult the full text for CNV coordinates, the number of COL4A2 carriers, segregation, and validation (MLPA, qPCR, Nanopore).

Only the title and abstract were available. This is a registry survey study (Gould Syndrome Foundation Registry) of 71 children with COL4A1 (n=59) or COL4A2 (n=12) variants. The abstract names no specific variants and gives no variant-level genotype data. It reports aggregate phenotypes: cerebral palsy 54%, epilepsy 42%, stroke 48%, and antenatal stroke in 11 patients (15%), which was associated with Cesarean delivery (p=0.016). The full text or supplement may list individual variants; that material was not provided.

variants.phenotype_details: Adult-onset CSVD: ischemic and hemorrhagic events, motor impairment, cognitive decline; MRI with extensive white matter hyperintensities, lacunes (particularly pontine), microbleeds, and in some cases saccular aneurysms or arterial dolichoectasia. Only 2 probands had a positive family history of CSVD.
variants.reported_classification: pathogenic (authors state the series confirms pathogenicity of COL4A1/2 duplications and triplications)
evidence_quotes: We report 7 adult probands carrying duplications or triplications of COL4A1 and COL4A2, in whom no pathogenic variants were identified in other known CSVD genes.
Genomic rearrangements ranged from 328 kb to 11.8 Mb, involving complete or partial duplication/triplication of COL4A1/2.

Brain magnetic resonance imaging consistently showed extensive white matter hyperintensities, lacunes (particularly in the pons), microbleeds, and, in some cases, saccular aneurysms or arterial dolichoectasia.
Only 2 probands had a positive family history of CSVD.
variants.notes: Aggregate record: the abstract describes 7 distinct copy number gains (duplications or triplications, 328 kb to 11.8 Mb at 13q33q34) spanning both COL4A1 and COL4A2, but gives no per-proband coordinates, breakpoints, dosage (dup vs trip) or inheritance. These are 7 different rearrangements and should be split into individual records from the full text. The gene field is set to COL4A1 only because one value is required; the CNVs involve COL4A2 as well. n_families assumes one family per proband. Two probands had a positive family history, but segregation and parental testing are not described, so all 7 are counted as inheritance unknown. The screened cohort size is not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The full text presumably gives the individual CNV coordinates, dosage and per-patient phenotypes, so a curator should replace the single aggregate CNV record with per-proband records. Some of the 7 probands may overlap with earlier reports of COL4A1/2 duplications, but this cannot be judged from the abstract.

Only the title and abstract were available. Whole exome sequencing was performed in 191 individuals: 63 migraine, 62 epilepsy, 39 comorbid, 16 unaffected first-degree relatives and 11 healthy controls. The abstract states that in the migraine-epilepsy comorbidity group, alterations were observed in 'other gene (COL4A1)'. It does not name the specific COL4A1 variant, its HGVS nomenclature, the number of carriers, the inheritance, the ACMG classification or the individual phenotypes. Because no specific variant could be identified, no variant record was created. The full text, and any supplementary tables, should be reviewed to extract the COL4A1 variant or variants found in the comorbid group, using a denominator of 39 comorbid cases within 191 sequenced individuals.

Abstract only. Chromosomal microarray and exome sequencing were performed in 61 individuals with CP secondary to perinatal cerebrovascular injury (37 ischemic, 24 hemorrhagic). The abstract states that three hemorrhagic cases carried (likely) pathogenic COL4A1 variants. It does not name the specific variants, their inheritance, or individual phenotypes beyond perinatal hemorrhagic brain injury with CP. No variant records were created because the variants are not identified. The abstract does not say whether the three cases share a variant or carry distinct ones. The full text should be obtained to extract the three COL4A1 variants; the denominator is 61 tested, or 24 in the hemorrhagic subgroup. The other diagnoses are not relevant to COL4A1/COL4A2: a de novo 12pter duplication and a mosaic JAG1 variant.

evidence_quotes: A 21-year-old female developed two stroke episodes involving hemiparesis and ocular palsy.
Head imaging revealed recurrent supra- and infratentorial ischemic and hemorrhagic brain injuries, subcortical microbleeds and white matter lesions.
Porencephalic ventricle dysmorphology was also obvious.
Genetic analyses revealed a novel, likely pathogenic missense variant in the triple-helical region of COL4A1 not detectable in the patient's parents.
variants.notes: Abstract only; the specific nucleotide/protein change is not given, so the affected residue is unknown (variant_type set to missense_other only because it is described as missense; it may in fact be a glycine substitution). De novo status based on trio-exome sequencing with variant absent in both parents; parentage confirmation not described in the abstract.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. The abstract does not name the COL4A1 variant (no HGVS or transcript), so the record cannot be matched to other reports; full text needed to obtain the exact variant.

Abstract only. This is a systematic review of cerebral palsy genetic studies published 2010-2024. COL4A1 is named as one of 6 tier I genes. No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants or new individuals are reported in the abstract, so no variant records were created.

Abstract only. WGS was performed in 327 children with cerebral palsy and their parents. The abstract states that 'The COL4A1 gene had the most P/LP SNVs', but it names no specific variants and gives no carrier count, inheritance or phenotype for individual carriers, so no variant records were created. The full text and supplementary tables probably list the COL4A1 P/LP variants found in the CP probands (trio design, so likely de novo or inherited status). A curator should retrieve the full text to extract them.

Only the title and abstract were available. The abstract describes exome sequencing of 8 patients from 6 families with presumed perinatal stroke in Saudi Arabia. It says a likely deleterious variant was found in four families, in genes including COL4A2, JAM3, ESAM and NID1. The abstract does not give the COL4A2 variant's nomenclature, the number of carriers or families, inheritance, zygosity or phenotype details. For that reason no variant record was created. The full text should be reviewed to extract the specific COL4A2 variant, which is likely in one family out of 6 families and 8 patients tested. Inheritance may be recessive given the consanguineous Saudi setting, but this is unverified. has_variant_level_data is set to true because the paper appears to report a specific COL4A2 variant in a specific family, although that detail is not in the abstract.

variants.phenotype_details: 12-month-old girl with drug-resistant focal epilepsy with daily seizures from age 2 months; left occipital focal cortical dysplasia (histopathology FCD type Ia); mild right-sided hemiparesis and developmental delay. Seizure free after left occipital lobectomy, with improved cognitive and motor development.
evidence_quotes: This case illustrates successful resective epilepsy surgery in a 12-month-old girl with left occipital focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) associated with a heterozygous splice-donor variant in COL4A1.

She presented with drug-resistant focal epilepsy with daily seizures from the age of 2 months, refractory to several combinations of antiseizure medications, as well as mild right-sided hemiparesis and developmental delay.
Histopathology of the resected brain tissue showed FCD type Ia.
variants.notes: Abstract only; exact c./p. nomenclature of the splice-donor variant not given in the abstract. Inheritance not described. Hemiparesis is attributed to the cortical dysplasia/epileptogenic lesion, not explicitly to perinatal haemorrhage, so cerebrovascular was not listed; FCD, epilepsy and developmental delay classified as other.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. The specific COL4A1 splice-donor variant (described as novel) is not named in the abstract; full text needed for HGVS nomenclature, inheritance and any additional imaging findings (e.g., small vessel or haemorrhagic lesions).

Abstract only. This is a retrospective case series of eight patients with fetal intraparenchymal hemorrhage and COL4A1/A2 variants. The abstract does not name any specific variants, does not say which gene (COL4A1 vs COL4A2) is affected in each patient, and gives no inheritance data, so no variant-level records can be created. The full text, which likely contains a per-patient variant table, would be needed. Aggregate phenotypes reported in the abstract: IPH in all 8 patients (frontal lobes in all; basal ganglia in 6/8; multifocal and bilateral in 4/8); ventriculomegaly in all; IVH in 4/8; postnatal follow-up available in 5.

Abstract only. This is a cohort study of 520 participants with neurodegenerative diseases from the ONDRI study. It determined carrier status of rare non-synonymous variants in ABCC6, COL4A1/COL4A2 and NOTCH3/HTRA1. The abstract names no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants and gives no carrier counts or individual-level data. It reports significant SVD imaging associations only for NOTCH3/HTRA1. The full text or supplement may list individual COL4A1/COL4A2 variants and carriers; these should be reviewed if available.

Abstract only. The paper is a retrospective review of 60 children referred to a Kidney Genomics Clinic with haematuria. COL4A1 was included in a limited haematuria panel (COL4A1, COL4A3, COL4A4, COL4A5, MYH9). The abstract reports no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants and does not say whether any diagnoses were attributable to COL4A1. The full text may contain variant-level data and should be checked.

Abstract only. COL4A1 is listed among eight candidate genes in a cohort of 20 Vietnamese children with West syndrome screened by NGS, but the abstract does not give the specific COL4A1 variant, its classification, inheritance, or the carrier's phenotype. No variant-level record could be created; full text needed to extract the COL4A1 variant (cohort n_tested=20).

Abstract only. The study used a targeted NGS panel of 15 Mendelian stroke genes, including COL4A1, to screen 1,033 young stroke/TIA patients (≤55 years). Among them, 131 patients carried 28 clinically relevant genetic variants (CRGVs), most often in RNF213, ABCC6 and NOTCH3. The abstract names no specific COL4A1 variant and gives no COL4A1 carrier count. COL4A2 was not on the panel. Any COL4A1 findings would be in the full text or supplement, which were not provided.

Abstract only. The paper describes one family with recessive (biallelic) COL4A2 pathogenic variants and a neuroimaging phenotype of leukoencephalopathy with spot-like calcifications. The specific variants, the number of affected individuals, zygosity (homozygous vs compound heterozygous) and parental carrier status are not given in the abstract. No variant record was created; a curator should consult the full text to extract the COL4A2 variants (expected: 1 family, recessive inheritance, small_vessel phenotype).

Abstract only. The paper is about PITX2 and FOXC1 in Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome. COL4A1 is mentioned only in the literature review summary: 'six families with variants in ADAMTS17, PRDM5, COL4A1 or CYP1B1'. These families appear to come from previously published reports. The abstract gives no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant and does not say how many of the six families carry COL4A1 variants. The new probands in this study had FOXC1 or PITX2 variants. The full text and supplementary review tables may list COL4A1 families from prior literature, but they were not provided.

Only the title and abstract were available. This pilot study ran trio genome sequencing on 13 fetal congenital heart defect trios. The abstract states that findings included 'pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in DNAH5, COL4A1, PTPN11, and KRAS' among the 4/13 diagnosed fetuses, which implies one fetus (n_tested = 13 trios) carries a COL4A1 P/LP variant. However, the abstract does not give the variant nomenclature, the inheritance or the fetus's specific phenotype beyond complex CHD and other structural anomalies. No specific variant could therefore be recorded. The full text should be reviewed to extract the COL4A1 variant, its inheritance (trio data likely available) and the fetal phenotype.

Abstract only. This is a cohort of 55 Argentine subjects with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy studied by targeted gene panel and whole exome sequencing. The abstract states that novel variants were identified in COL4A1, among other genes, after re-interpretation and re-analysis. It does not give the specific COL4A1 variant, the number of carriers, inheritance or phenotype details. The full text and tables would be needed to extract a variant-level record. The denominator would be 55 subjects.

Abstract only. This is a retrospective single-center cohort of 18 fetuses selected from 956 cases of fetal cerebral anomaly. Findings in the abstract: five fetuses had a pathogenic COL4A1 mutation, four of them de novo. Four fetuses had a variant of unknown significance, one in COL4A1 and three in COL4A2. The specific variants (HGVS) are not named in the abstract, so no variant-level records could be created. The full text likely contains a table of the individual variants and should be reviewed. Phenotypes were severe and/or multifocal hemorrhagic or ischemic-hemorrhagic fetal cerebral lesions, with or without schizencephaly or porencephaly. Median gestational age at diagnosis was 24 weeks in cases with a mutation.

However, COL4A2 may have also contributed to the development of pial AVF because the COL4A2 and RASA1 variants have a common pathophysiology, wherein the patient develops lesions due to collagen type IV deficiency.
variants.notes: Abstract only: the specific COL4A2 variant (nomenclature, type, transcript), inheritance and full phenotype are not given. Co-occurring RASA1 variant considered the primary cause by the authors; COL4A2 contribution is speculative. Pial AVF placed under 'other' as it is a vascular malformation not matching the listed cerebrovascular examples; a curator may prefer 'cerebrovascular'.

The paper reports a single adult patient with pial AVF/CM-AVM carrying both a RASA1 variant and a COL4A2 variant, but the COL4A2 variant is not specified in the abstract; full text needed to record the variant name, type, inheritance and classification.

Abstract only. This is a WES study of 26 probands from 25 families with unexplained perinatal intracranial hemorrhage. The abstract states that causative or likely causative variants were found in 4 subjects from 3 of the 25 families, in COL4A1, COL4A2 and TREX-1. It does not name the specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants, how many families carry each gene, the inheritance of each, or the phenotypes of individual carriers. The overall statement that 55% of variants were inherited from an asymptomatic parent is not attributed to any one gene. No variant records were created because no variant notation is given. The full text should be reviewed to extract the COL4A1 and COL4A2 variants, with n_tested = 26 probands (25 families).

Systematic review of extracerebral phenotypes in monogenic cSVD (COL4A1/2, TREX1, HTRA1, ADA2, CTSA). Only the title and abstract were available. The abstract gives aggregate counts from the literature: 96 COL4A1 publications covering 350 individuals and 16 COL4A2 publications covering 37 individuals. Extracerebral phenotypes were reported in 47% of COL4A1 and 14% of COL4A2 individuals. No specific variants are named and no new individuals are reported, so no variant records were created.

Abstract only. A 15-gene targeted panel was run on 38 patients with pediatric/perinatal stroke. Pathogenic variants in ABCC6 and COL4A1 were found in 4 patients (10.5%). The abstract does not name the specific COL4A1 variants and does not say how many of the 4 patients carry COL4A1 rather than ABCC6 variants. It also gives no inheritance or per-patient phenotype. No variant-level record could be created; the full text is needed to extract the COL4A1 variants (denominator n_tested = 38).

Abstract only. This is a cohort of 218 individuals with suspected COL4A1/2-related brain defects. Pathogenic COL4A1/2 variants were found in 56 (porencephaly 29, schizencephaly 12, other 15), and 34 of these were de novo. Foetal abnormalities were reported in 32 of the 47 with foetal information. The abstract names no specific variants and does not split them by gene (COL4A1 vs COL4A2), so no variant-level records can be extracted. The full text or supplementary tables likely list the individual variants. This cohort may overlap with earlier reports from the same group (Japanese cohorts of COL4A1/2 porencephaly and schizencephaly).

Abstract only. The paper describes five patients with heterozygous COL4A1 variants and West syndrome, periventricular leukomalacia and microcephaly. Three were examined by the authors and two were previously reported. The abstract does not name any specific variant, so no variant-level records could be created. The full text should be reviewed to obtain the variants, inheritance (parental testing) and phenotype details for the three new patients, and to identify which two patients overlap with prior reports.

A single fetus with a COL4A1 variant (not specified) is mentioned, presenting with fetal anemia secondary to cerebral hemorrhages. No specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants or carriers are described in the abstract. The full text or supplement may list COL4A1 variants contributing to the burden signal, but these were not provided.

Abstract only. All reported variants are in COLGALT1 (c.452T>G p.Leu151Arg, c.1096delG p.Glu366Argfs*15, c.460G>C p.Ala154Pro, c.1129G>C p.Gly377Arg), found in 2 unrelated patients with suspected COL4A1/COL4A2-related disorders. COL4A1 appears only in the functional readout: COLGALT1 knockdown altered COL4A1 secretion, and mutant COLGALT1 did not fully restore it in rescue experiments. The full text may describe prior negative COL4A1/COL4A2 screening of these patients, but that cannot be confirmed from the abstract.

variants.phenotype_details: Cerebral small vessel disease / PADMAL (pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy with leukoencephalopathy), described as a severe early onset ischemic cSVD; MRI showed multiple pontine infarcts in all symptomatic mutation carriers. Specific ages at onset not given in abstract.
variants.functional_evidence: RT-qPCR of patients' primary fibroblasts and luciferase reporter assays indicated COL4A1 upregulation through disrupted miR-29 binding to its target site.
variants.prior_report_reason: One of the probands came from the first reported PADMAL family, which was described in an earlier publication.
evidence_quotes: A candidate heterozygous variant located in a predicted miR-29 microRNA binding site, within the 3' untranslated region of COL4A1, was identified in the large French cSVD family.
Five additional unrelated probands, including the PADMAL proband, harbored heterozygous variants in this microRNA binding site.

The identified candidate gene was then screened in 202 cSVD unrelated probands, including 1 proband from the first reported pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy with leukoencephalopathy (PADMAL) family.
Magnetic resonance imaging features were characterized by the presence of multiple pontine infarcts in all symptomatic mutation carriers.
RT-qPCR analyses of patients' primary fibroblasts and luciferase reporter assays strongly favor an upregulation of COL4A1 mediated by disruption of miR-29 binding to its target site.
variants.notes: Abstract only. This is an aggregate record: the abstract says 'variants' (plural) within the miR-29 binding site of the COL4A1 3'UTR but names none of them, so the number of distinct variants and their HGVS names are unknown. The curator should split this record by variant from the full text. n_probands is 6: the French index family plus 5 additional probands. n_tested of 202 is the screening cohort for the 5 additional probands; the index family was identified separately by linkage analysis and exome sequencing. The abstract states that the variants cosegregated with the affected phenotype in relatives, but gives no per-proband parental status, so inheritance is recorded as unknown.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The specific 3'UTR variant nomenclature, per-family segregation data, carrier counts and ages at onset are presumably in the full text, which was not provided. A case-control comparison of variant burden within the binding site was reported (p = 1.77 × 10E-12), but this concerns rare causal variants, not association SNPs.

GeneReviews chapter (COL4A1-Related Disorders); only the title and abstract were provided. The abstract summarises the clinical spectrum, diagnosis, management and genetic counselling (autosomal dominant inheritance, at least 27% de novo) but reports no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in specific individuals. Any variant tables in the full chapter were not available.

Review article on monogenic causes of stroke and cerebral small vessel disease; only the title and abstract were available. COL4A1/COL4A2-related arteriopathy is mentioned generally. No specific variants are reported in specific individuals.

variants.phenotype_details: Congenital cataract diagnosed at 3 months, with normal brain MRI at that time; over following years: focal epilepsy, mild diplegia, asymptomatic microhematuria, raised creatine kinase, MRI white matter abnormalities, and brain calcification on CT; brain lesions progressively decreased in extent and intensity on follow-up. Onset in infancy.
evidence_quotes: Here we report on the case of a patient carrying a novel de novo splicing mutation of COL4A1 associated with a distinctive clinical picture characterized by onset in infancy and an unusual evolution of the neuroradiological features.
At three months of age, the child was diagnosed with a congenital cataract, while his brain MRI was normal.

Over the following years, the patient developed focal epilepsy, mild diplegia, asymptomatic microhematuria, raised creatine kinase levels, MRI white matter abnormalities and brain calcification on CT.
variants.notes: Abstract only; exact variant nomenclature not given. Called de novo but parental testing not described in abstract, so recorded as assumed. Proband also carries a second, paternally inherited COL4A1 variant (possible compound heterozygosity), so phenotype cannot be attributed to this variant alone. Assignment of diplegia to cerebrovascular is an interpretation based on title ('early postnatal cerebrovascular events').
