evidence_quotes: The significance of a second variant in COL4A1 carried by the child and inherited from his father remains to be clarified.
In conclusion, our patient shows new aspects of this collagenopathy and possibly a COL4A1 compound heterozygosity.
variants.notes: Abstract only; variant identity and type not stated. Phenotypes listed are those of the proband, who also carries the de novo splice variant; authors consider this variant's significance unclear. Total carriers of 2 assumes father is a carrier as stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. Neither COL4A1 variant is named in the abstract (no HGVS). Single proband carries two COL4A1 variants: a de novo splice variant and a paternally inherited variant of uncertain significance; authors suggest possible compound heterozygosity. Full text needed for nomenclature, parental testing details, and father's phenotype.

Abstract only. The paper reports a cysteine-to-serine point mutation in COL4A5 (alpha 5(IV) collagen) in Alport syndrome in Utah Kindred P, not a COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant. The mention of the conserved cysteine across all type IV collagen alpha chains is a general statement and does not describe a COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant in any individual. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 records were created.

Abstract only. This is a narrative review of COL4A1/2-related cerebral small vessel disease. The abstract mentions 'illustrative multigenerational cases' to show genotype-phenotype correlation, but it names no specific variants or individuals. The full text may describe specific variants in these families and should be checked by a curator.

Abstract-only input. This is a narrative review of hereditary cerebral small vessel disease. It mentions COL4A1/2-associated microangiopathies only as a disease category. No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants and no individual patients are reported.

Abstract only. This is a systematic review of 99 previously published articles covering 367 patients with COL4A1/COL4A2-related disorders. It reports aggregate phenotype frequencies: neurologic 78.5%, ocular 71.3%, renal 15.5%, muscular 17.8% and cardiovascular 7.9%. The abstract names no specific variants, and the review reports no new individuals. All patients come from prior publications, so no variant records were created.

Abstract only. The paper describes three clinical cases with prenatal presentation and pathogenic COL4A1 mutations, but the abstract does not name the specific variants, their inheritance or their per-patient phenotypes. No variant records were created. The full text should be reviewed to extract the three cases' variants, inheritance and phenotypes (CNS malformations such as porencephaly, schizencephaly and hydranencephaly).

variants.phenotype_details: Proband: 44-year-old man with lacunar infarction; his father also had a lacunar infarction. Brain MRI showed multiple white matter hyperintensities and abnormal elongation and tortuosity (dolichoectasia) of the internal carotid and vertebrobasilar arteries.
evidence_quotes: Here, we report a Japanese family with this duplication along with dilation and tortuosity in the multiple intracranial arteries.
A 44-year-old man and his father experienced a lacunar infarction.
Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple white matter hyperintensities and abnormal elongation and tortuosity of the ICA/VA.
Genetic studies revealed a distal duplication at 13q34.
variants.notes: Abstract only. This is a copy-number duplication, not a deletion; deletion_cnv is the closest allowed type. The duplication spans both COL4A1 and COL4A2; it is recorded once under COL4A1 to avoid duplicating one variant. Duplication size and breakpoints are not given. The abstract does not explicitly state that the father was tested. Paternal inheritance (inh_inherited) and 2 total carriers are inferred from the plural 'patients ... with COL4A1/COL4A2 duplication' in the title and from 'Our cases'.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. A single Japanese family carries a 13q34 duplication that includes COL4A1 and COL4A2. Details such as duplication coordinates, segregation testing and other family members may be in the full text, which was not provided.

Abstract only. This is an iPSC functional and drug-screening study using cells derived from patients with HTRA1 or COL4A1/2 mutations. The abstract names no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant, gives no patient counts or phenotypes for the COL4A1/2 donors, and does not say which of the two genes is involved. The full text may give donor variants; if it does, it would need a separate extraction.

variants.as_written: a duplication in the region of chromosome 13, which included the COL4A1 and COL4A2 genes
variants.phenotype_details: First ischemic stroke at age 51; MRI showed extensive acute and chronic lacunar infarcts and white matter hyperintensities across both hemispheres, involving the anterior temporal lobe and external capsule; bilateral thalamic microbleeds; CADASIL-like clinical and MRI picture.
evidence_quotes: Targeted NGS and CNV-seq analysis identified a duplication in the region of chromosome 13, which included the COL4A1 and COL4A2 genes.
The patient experienced his first ischemic stroke at age 51.

Cranial MRI revealed extensive acute and chronic lacunar infarcts and white matter hyperintensities across both cerebral hemispheres, with involvement of the anterior temporal lobe and the external capsule.
Bilateral thalamic microbleeds were also noted.
variants.notes: Copy-number gain (duplication), not a deletion; recorded as deletion_cnv because it is the only CNV category available. A single duplication spanning both COL4A1 and COL4A2 in one patient, recorded once under COL4A1 to avoid double-counting the proband. Exact breakpoints, size and coordinates are not given in the abstract. Inheritance and family testing are not described in the abstract. n_tested=1 reflects a single-case report.

extraction.extraction_notes: Abstract only. The single CNV (a 13q duplication encompassing both COL4A1 and COL4A2) is recorded as one COL4A1 record; the same event also involves COL4A2, and a curator may wish to cross-index it under COL4A2. The duplication size, breakpoints and segregation are likely to be in the full text, which was not provided.

variants.as_written: insertion of a mobile genetic element in the COL4A1 gene
variants.phenotype_details: Novel hereditary cerebral small vessel disease; no further clinical details or ages of onset given in the abstract.
variants.prior_report_reason: The abstract describes the disease and insertion as 'recently identified' in 10 families, implying these families were reported in an earlier publication; this study re-analyses their probands for haplotype sharing.
evidence_quotes: A novel genetic cerebral small vessel disease, linked to the insertion of a mobile genetic element in the COL4A1 gene has recently been identified.
Notably, 8 out of the 10 families carrying this mutation were known to come from Brittany, a specific region in France, suggesting the possibility of a common ancestor and a founder effect.
Probands from each of the 10 families were analyzed with high-density single nucleotide polymorphism arrays.
Furthermore, all probands shared a common identical-by-descent haplotype around the COL4A1 locus on 13q34, establishing the inheritance of the mutation from a single common ancestor.
variants.notes: Abstract only. The insertion is named as an AluYa5 insertion in the conclusions; its exact location (e.g., UTR or intron) and HGVS are not stated. Two of the 10 families were shown to be closely related, so they may not be fully independent. The families are familial, but parental carrier status per proband is not described, so inheritance is recorded as unknown. These are pre-identified carrier families rather than a screened cohort, so no screening denominator is given.

extraction.extraction_notes: Abstract only. This is a founder or identity-by-descent haplotype study of 10 previously identified families carrying a COL4A1 AluYa5 insertion. The families very likely overlap with the original report of this disease, which is not cited by name in the abstract. Founder age is estimated at about 1735 (95% CI, 1600-1820).

Abstract only. The study assessed retinal arteriolar tortuosity in 52 eyes of 28 patients carrying COL4A1 or COL4A2 mutations. Eyes were grouped as normal (19), moderately increased tortuosity (13) or typical abnormal tortuosity (20). The abstract names no specific variants and does not split patients by gene, so no variant-level records can be created. Variant details may be in the full text, which was not provided.

Abstract only. This exome study enrolled 113 fetuses with intracranial hemorrhage, and all of them had already tested negative for COL4A1/A2. The causative genes it reports are MPL, MECOM, PROC, ESAM, ATP5PO, COQ2 and PDHA1. COL4A1/A2 appear only as background: an approximate 20% diagnostic yield in prior FICH referrals. The abstract names no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in individuals.

Abstract only. This is a pharmacogenetic association study of 7 SNPs in COL4A2, TNF, WNK2 and IL6, genotyped in 217 ICH patients with or without edaravone treatment. The COL4A2 SNPs are not named in the abstract and showed no reported association. The only significant hits, IL6 rs1800796 and WNK2 rs16936752, are association SNPs in other genes. No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific individuals as a candidate cause of disease, so no records were created.

Abstract only. The paper reports two cases of COL4A1-related disorder mimicking congenital TORCH infection, but the abstract does not name the specific variants, inheritance or individual phenotypes, so no variant records were created. The full text likely contains variant-level data (the title mentions an expanded genotype spectrum) and should be reviewed by a curator.

variants.phenotype_details: 64-year-old male with late-onset ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhages, microbleeds, bilateral symmetrical leukoencephalopathy (diffuse white matter changes), recurrence over a short period, and bilateral retinopathy. Family history of brain aneurysm, kidney diseases and early-onset stroke; relatives' carrier status not stated.
evidence_quotes: A 64-year-old male was found to have an ischemic stroke and diffuse white matter changes.
Genetic testing revealed COL4A1 gene mutation of heterozygous Alu insertion at intron 16.

Our case has attributes consistent with a heritable leukoencephalopathy: (1) late-onset presentation, (2) intracerebral hemorrhages and microbleeds, (3) bilateral symmetrical leukoencephalopathy, (4) recurrence over a short period of time, (5) bilateral retinopathy, and (6) family history notable for brain aneurysm, kidney diseases, and early-onset stroke.
variants.notes: Abstract only. Exact insertion position, HGVS nomenclature, transcript, and any splicing effect not given. Parental/family segregation testing not described; family history suggestive but inheritance unknown. Kidney disease reported only in relatives of unknown genotype, so renal not listed. Authors state Alu insertion not previously reported in COL4A1 syndromes.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. Single case report of a COL4A1 intron 16 Alu insertion; variant details (precise coordinates, transcript, functional/RNA studies) may be in the full text, which was not provided.

Abstract only. This is a study of ameloblastoma tumour biology. COL4A2 was identified as an 'essential gene' through whole-exome sequencing of 5 AB patients and microarray datasets, and was found upregulated in tumour tissue. The abstract reports no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variant in any individual. The findings are expression-level and functional (decellularized ECM effects on PDLSC osteogenesis), not germline variant evidence.

Abstract only. This is a retrospective cohort of 57 fetuses with fetal intracranial hemorrhage diagnosed by fetal MRI at Children's National Hospital, 2012-2020. The abstract says one case had a 'COL4A1 mutation' as the identified etiology: 'two had genetic findings (fetal neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia and COL4A1 mutation)'. No specific variant (c./p. notation), inheritance, or individual-level phenotype is given, so no variant record was created. The full text may name the variant and give details on that case (n_tested would be 57; phenotype would be fetal ICH, cerebrovascular). A curator should check the full text.

Only the title and abstract were available. The paper describes eight COL4A1-mutated fetuses with prenatally detected cerebral haemorrhages, all ending in elective termination of pregnancy. It reports supra- and infratentorial multifocal haemorrhagic lesions, post-ischemic damage, vascular dilation and hypervascularization. The abstract does not name any specific COL4A1 variant, inheritance or parental testing, so no variant records could be created. The full text likely contains the variant-level data (8 fetal cases, cerebrovascular phenotype) and should be reviewed by a curator.

Abstract only. This is a patient registry report (Gould Syndrome Global Registry): 70 families and 100 affected people (40 adults, 60 children), with a subanalysis of 35 of the 60 children focused on epilepsy. The abstract does not name any specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant in any specific individual, so no variant records were created. The full text may contain variant-level data that was not provided here.

Abstract only. This is a systematic review of somatic tumor sequencing in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (279 patients pooled from prior studies). COL4A1 and COL4A2 are mentioned only as genes whose somatic mutations correlate with demographic characteristics or are newly noted in SCC. The abstract names no specific germline variants and does not link any variant to individual patients, so no variant records were created.

Abstract only. The paper describes four fetal autopsy cases of COL4A1-related disease confirmed by genetic sequencing. The phenotypes include ventricular zone hemorrhage, CNS small vessel thrombosis, schizencephaly with arteriopathy and cerebral infarcts, and placental fetal vascular malperfusion. The abstract does not name any specific COL4A1 variants (no c./p. nomenclature) and gives no inheritance information. As a result, no variant-level records could be created. The full text may contain the specific variants per case and should be reviewed by a curator.

Abstract only. This is a nasopharyngeal carcinoma tumour WES/transcriptome study. COL4A1 appears only as a differentially expressed 'potentially subtype relevant gene' identified from expression data (GSE12452). The abstract reports no specific germline COL4A1/COL4A2 variant in any individual, so no variant records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: 18-year-old girl with intellectual disability and stroke (hemorrhagic); MRI basal ganglia microbleeds, periventricular white matter signal changes, porencephalic cyst; bilateral microcornea and Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly; autopsy showed hemorrhagic lesions at multiple brain sites and thickened small-caliber vessels with basement membrane disruption and fragmentation.
evidence_quotes: We report a rare case of stroke in an intellectually disabled 18-year-old girl with radiological evidence of basal ganglia microbleeds, periventricular white matter signal changes and porencephalic cyst.
Ophthalmic examination revealed bilateral microcornea and Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly.
A missense COL4A1 mutation involving glycine residue was detected in the patient.
variants.notes: Abstract only; the exact variant (c./p. nomenclature, transcript) is not given in the abstract, only described as a glycine missense. Inheritance/parental testing not described. Histopathology (collagen IV alpha 1 IHC and EM showing basement membrane disruption) is patient tissue pathology, not variant-specific functional assay. n_tested set to 1 as a single-patient case report.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. The specific COL4A1 variant is not named in the abstract; curator should consult full text for exact nomenclature, transcript and inheritance.

Abstract only. The paper reports 2 infants with COL4A1 mutations presenting with congenital posterior cortical cataracts, bilateral posterior lenticonus and porencephaly, but the abstract does not name the specific variants or give inheritance. No variant records could be created. The full text should be reviewed to obtain the variant nomenclature, inheritance and phenotypes (cerebrovascular: porencephaly; ocular: congenital cataract, posterior lenticonus) for the 2 probands.

Abstract only. This is a case report of a 9-month-old boy with schizencephaly, a congenital cataract and progressive hydrocephalus. He developed malignant hyperthermia and cerebral venous thrombosis after a ventriculoperitoneal shunt. The abstract states only that 'Genetic testing revealed a germline COL4A1 mutation'. It does not give the specific variant, its HGVS nomenclature or its inheritance (de novo vs inherited). For that reason no variant record was created. The full text probably names the variant and should be checked by a curator. If it does, expect one proband and one family, with phenotype systems cerebrovascular (schizencephaly, cerebral venous thrombosis), ocular (congenital cataract) and other (hydrocephalus, postoperative malignant hyperthermia).

Abstract only. The paper retrospectively reviewed MRI data of 18 COL4A1 mutation carriers. It reports polymicrogyria in two patients and schizencephaly in the mother of a further patient (three new cases). No specific variant nomenclature is given in the abstract, so no variant-level records could be created. The full text likely lists the specific COL4A1 variants and should be reviewed by a curator.

Abstract only. Clinicopathologic study of 20 lymphomatoid papulosis cases with whole exome sequencing of 2 type C cases. COL4A1 is mentioned only as a gene involved in the extracellular matrix receptor pathway among 101 non-synonymous mutations, probably somatic or tumor-derived. No specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is named, and no germline variant is assigned to an individual. Not relevant to COL4A1/COL4A2 germline disease; no variant-level data.

Abstract only. The paper is a single case report of a 4-year-old girl with a de novo COL4A1 mutation. Her phenotype was drug-resistant epilepsy and epileptic encephalopathy, hemiplegia and developmental delay, with no porencephaly on MRI and no cataract or renal abnormality. She was seizure free after functional hemispherectomy with no intracranial hemorrhage. The specific COL4A1 variant (c./p. nomenclature) is not given in the abstract, so no variant-level record was created. The abstract also does not describe parental testing; de novo status is asserted only. A curator with the full text should add a record for this proband: n_probands=1, de novo (confirm whether parental testing was done), phenotype systems likely 'other' (epilepsy, developmental delay) plus possibly 'cerebrovascular' if the hemiplegia is attributed to perinatal injury.

Abstract-only input for a systematic review of hereditary cerebral small vessel disease. It mentions collagen type IV mutations (including PADMAL) only generally. The abstract reports no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants or individuals.

variants.phenotype_details: Term infant (neonate) with encephalomalacia, extensive intrauterine stroke and anterior segment dysgenesis.
evidence_quotes: We describe a term infant with encephalomalacia, extensive intrauterine stroke and anterior segment dysgenesis with a de novo mutation in COL4A1.
variants.notes: Abstract only; the specific COL4A1 variant (nucleotide/protein change) is not given in the abstract, so variant_type is unknown and recorded as 'other'. De novo status stated but parental testing not described in the abstract, so counted as assumed. n_tested reflects a single-patient case report.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. The abstract reports one neonate with a de novo COL4A1 mutation but does not name the variant; the full text should be checked to obtain the exact HGVS designation, transcript, parental testing details and any additional phenotypes.

Abstract only. The paper reports diagnostic COL4A1/COL4A2 analysis in 183 index patients (Erasmus MC, 2005-2013), identifying 21 COL4A1 and 3 COL4A2 mutations, with a de novo rate of 40% (10/24), and clinical data on 13 novel families. However, the abstract names no specific variants, so no per-variant records could be created. The full text and tables would be needed to extract variant-level data. Some families may overlap with earlier reports from the same center.

Abstract only. The abstract reports that 7 of 154 adult-onset leukoencephalopathy patients (vascular group, n=55) carried a 'COL4A1 mutation', but no specific variants are named. Variant-level details are likely in the full text or tables, which were not provided. No records were created because no specific variant is identifiable.

Abstract-only input. This is a case report of one child with a COL4A1 mutation and schizencephaly. Susceptibility-weighted imaging showed hemorrhages at the periphery of the schizencephalic region, intraparenchymal hemorrhages and tortuous intracranial veins. The abstract does not name the variant (no c. or p. notation), its type, or its inheritance, so no VariantEvidence record was created. The full text likely gives the specific variant and should be checked by the curator. The phenotype would map to cerebrovascular (schizencephaly, intracranial hemorrhage).

variants.phenotype_details: Preterm infant with severe hemolytic jaundice requiring exchange transfusion just after birth (non-alloimmune, normal erythrocyte metabolism/membrane/hemoglobin tests, non-diagnostic bone marrow); porencephaly, epilepsy, elevated serum creatine kinase, persistent microscopic hematuria.
evidence_quotes: We report our experience with a preterm infant with severe hemolytic jaundice who required exchange transfusion just after birth.
The patient had several other complications, including porencephaly, epilepsy, elevated serum levels of creatine kinase, and persistent microscopic hematuria.
Later, we detected a genetic mutation in COL4A1, which was recently found to be associated with hemolytic anemia.
variants.notes: Abstract only; the specific variant (nucleotide/protein change), variant type and inheritance are not stated in the abstract. Title calls it a novel COL4A1 mutation. variant_type set to 'other' because the actual type is unknown.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. The abstract reports a single patient with a novel COL4A1 mutation but does not name the variant; the full text would be needed to obtain HGVS nomenclature, transcript, and parental testing results.

variants.phenotype_details: 29-year-old male with adult-onset recurrent deep intracerebral hemorrhages of different age causing mild motor and sensory hemisyndromes; diffuse leukoencephalopathy; multiple cerebral microbleeds; small bilateral aneurysms of the carotid siphon; nephropathy with significant microscopic hematuria; myopathy with elevated creatine kinase.
evidence_quotes: Herein, we report on a young adult patient with recurrent intracerebral hemorrhage, leukoencephalopathy, intracranial aneurysms, nephropathy, and myopathy associated with a novel COL4A2 mutation.
We extensively investigated a 29-year-old male patient with recurrent deep intracerebral hemorrhages causing mild motor and sensory hemisyndromes.
Brain MRI showed deep intracerebral hemorrhages of different age, diffuse leukoencephalopathy, multiple cerebral microbleeds and small aneurysms of the carotid siphon bilaterally.
Laboratory work-up revealed significant microscopic hematuria and elevation of creatine-kinase.
Genetic testing found a de novo glycine mutation within the COL4A2 triple helical domain.
variants.notes: Abstract only; the specific nucleotide/protein change is not given in the abstract. Called de novo but parental testing details not described in abstract, so recorded as assumed. Intracranial (carotid siphon) aneurysms noted in details; no separate token used.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only title and abstract available. The exact COL4A2 variant (HGVS) is not stated in the abstract; full text needed to identify the glycine substitution, transcript, and parental testing details.

Abstract only. The paper reports two cases of prenatal intracranial hemorrhage with cataract and links them to COL4A1. The abstract does not name any specific COL4A1 variants, give inheritance or describe parental testing. The full text likely contains variant-level data, so a curator should retrieve it to extract the two cases.

Abstract only. Four cases of antenatally detected fetal intraventricular hemorrhage were screened, with whole exome sequencing reported in the abstract. No pathological COL4A1 or COL4A2 mutations were found in any of the four patients. The paper reports no specific variants, so no variant records were created.

Abstract only. The study screened 71 patients (61 with porencephaly, 10 with schizencephaly) and found COL4A1 mutations in 15 of them: 10 missense, 1 nonsense, 1 frameshift and 3 splice site. Inheritance was 5 confirmed de novo, 1 cosegregating with familial porencephaly and 2 inherited from asymptomatic parents. RT-PCR showed aberrant splicing for 2 of the splice site mutations. Associated features included intracranial calcification, focal cortical dysplasia, pontocerebellar atrophy, ocular abnormalities, myopathy, elevated CK and hemolytic anemia. No individual variants are named in the abstract, so no variant-level records could be created. The full text, which is not provided, presumably lists all 15 mutations with per-patient phenotypes and should be curated.

Abstract only. This is a radiological phenotyping study of 119 patients with intracranial calcification. It mentions 3 patients with COL4A1-related disease, but the abstract names no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant. No variant-level data could be extracted. The full text may hold variant details for these 3 patients.

Abstract only. The paper reports three new COL4A1-related disease cases with raised creatine kinase and intracranial calcification. It also refers to five patients the authors previously described. No specific variants are named in the abstract, so no variant records could be created. The full text likely lists the variants and should be reviewed by a curator.

Abstract only. The paper describes four families (index cases: three male, one female) with childhood-presentation COL4A1 mutations. Three new pathogenic mutations are reported, and 11 affected family members span multiple generations in three families. The abstract does not name the specific variants, so no variant records could be created. Per-variant counts, inheritance and phenotypes need the full text. Reported phenotypes: childhood-onset stroke, infantile hemiplegia/spastic quadriplegia, infantile spasms, porencephaly, intracerebral haemorrhage, white matter change, congenital cataracts, anterior segment dysgenesis, microcephaly and developmental delay. Four families but only three new mutations: one family may carry a previously reported mutation.

variants.phenotype_details: Two siblings with porencephaly, hemiparesis and epilepsy; one sibling had an atrophic kidney. The carrier mother was asymptomatic but had an arachnoid cyst. The authors discuss a possible link between the atrophic kidney and arachnoid cyst and the mutation. No ages at onset are given in the abstract.
evidence_quotes: We describe two siblings with porencephaly, hemiparesis, epilepsy, atrophic kidney in one of the siblings and asymptomatic mothers with an arachnoid cyst.
We performed Col4A1 gene mutation screening and detected a novel mutation in mother and both of the children.
This family has some features previously undescribed in patients with mutations of Col4A1 gene like atrophic kidney in one sibling and arachnoid cyst in the mother.
variants.notes: Abstract only. The specific variant (nucleotide or protein change) is not named in the abstract, so the variant type is unknown and set to 'other'. One family is counted as one proband, inherited from the carrier mother; there are three carriers in total (mother and two children). Renal_hanac is listed only on the basis of an atrophic kidney whose attribution to the variant is speculative. Arachnoid cyst, epilepsy and hemiparesis are recorded under other/cerebrovascular as reported.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were available. The abstract describes a single family with a novel COL4A1 mutation but does not specify the variant. The full text would be needed to identify the variant, the transcript and any functional data.

Abstract only. The paper reports 5 patients with COL4A1 mutations and a characteristic pattern of intracranial calcification. Imaging showed periventricular leukomalacia-like changes, porencephaly, white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, and subependymal, deep white matter, basal ganglia and pontine calcification. No specific variants are named in the abstract, so no variant-level records were created. The full text likely lists the individual mutations; a curator should review it to extract the 5 variants and their inheritance. The denominator (size of the ongoing ICC study cohort) is not stated in the abstract.

Only the title and abstract were available. The paper describes 2 infants with fetal intracerebral haemorrhage, extensive hemispheric tissue loss (cerebellar tissue loss in one), and a COL4A1 mutation. The abstract does not name the specific variants, so no variant records could be created. The full text likely reports the variant designations, inheritance and possibly prior reports of these families; a curator should check it.

Review article on the clinical spectrum of COL4A1 mutations. Only the title and abstract were available. No specific variants are reported in specific individuals in the abstract, so no variant records were created.

Only the title and abstract were provided. The abstract reports three novel COL4A1 glycine missense substitutions in the collagenous domain, within the CB3[IV] fragment, in three families with HANAC syndrome. The abstract does not name the specific variants or say which family carries which variant, so no variant-level records were created. Phenotypes reported across the families were retinal arterial tortuosity and muscle cramps in common, with variable small vessel brain disease, Raynaud phenomena and kidney defects. Inheritance, carrier counts and phenotypes per family are presumably in the full text, which was not available. A curator should extract the three variants (one family each, n_families=1 each) from the full text.

Abstract only. This MRI study describes PADMAL in a large German family: 18 members were scanned and 6 had a pathological phenotype. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is named in the abstract. The genetic cause of PADMAL was later attributed to COL4A1 3'UTR (miR-29 binding site) variants in this family by subsequent publications, but that is not reported here.

Abstract only. This is a clinical and brain MRI follow-up of a single family with a COL4A1 mutation, but the abstract does not name the variant, so no variant record was created. Per the abstract, two affected members died from intracranial hemorrhage during a 7-year period. Four other carriers, aged 25-74, had no stroke, retinal hemorrhage, hematuria or dementia. On MRI, 3 of 4 had grade 3 diffuse leukoencephalopathy, all 4 had dilated perivascular spaces, and 3 of 4 had silent deep white-matter microbleeds, with no progression between baseline and follow-up. Because this is a 'follow-up study', the family was very likely reported before, possibly the French family described by Vahedi et al. and genotyped in Gould et al. 2006 (NEJM); this is unconfirmed. A curator should check the full text for the variant (HGVS) and the inheritance details, and should check for overlap with the prior report before adding a record.

Abstract only. The study screened 23 unrelated individuals with TBMN (index cases from 9 families plus 14 unrelated cases) for COL4A1/COL4A2 mutations using SSCA. No definite COL4A1 or COL4A2 mutations were identified. Novel polymorphisms were reported, but none are named in the abstract. Linkage analysis showed segregation with the COL4A1/COL4A2 locus in only 2 of 9 families. There are no variant-level data to extract.

variants.phenotype_details: Human family with small-vessel disease of the brain; no further detail or age at onset in the abstract.
evidence_quotes: We identified a COL4A1 mutation in a human family with small-vessel disease.
We concluded that mutation of COL4A1 may cause a spectrum of cerebrovascular phenotypes and that persons with COL4A1 mutations may be predisposed to hemorrhage, especially after environmental stress.
variants.notes: Abstract only. The specific variant is not named in the provided text, so hgvs fields are left empty and variant_type is set to 'other'. The full paper is generally cited as reporting COL4A1 G562E (p.Gly562Glu) in a family previously described clinically, possibly the Vahedi et al. family with infantile hemiparesis, retinal arteriolar tortuosity and leukoencephalopathy. This cannot be verified from the input, so same_family_as_prior_report is left false and the curator should check it. The family's inheritance pattern and carrier count are not stated in the abstract.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only the title and abstract were provided. Most of the paper is a mouse Col4a1 mutant study: intracerebral hemorrhage in newborn and adult mice, alleviated by surgical delivery. That mouse work concerns the mouse allele, not the human variant. The human variant identity, the family structure, the number of affected carriers and any segregation data are not available in the input. A single low-confidence record was created for the one human family mentioned.

Abstract only. This is a mouse study of three ENU-induced dominant Col4a1 alleles (Bru and Svc, both glycine substitutions in the Gly-Xaa-Yaa repeat; Raw, a Yaa-residue substitution). It reports no human patients, so no variant-level records were created. The specific amino-acid changes are not given in the abstract. The mouse phenotypes are: in Bru heterozygotes, Axenfeld-Rieger-like anterior segment dysgenesis, vacuolar cataracts, buphthalmos, optic nerve cupping and peripheral glomerulopathy; in Raw, a silvery appearance of the retinal arterioles. These may be useful as functional or model evidence for curators.

Abstract only. The paper characterises a mouse Col4a1 semidominant mutation (porencephaly, perinatal cerebral hemorrhage; inhibits secretion of mutant and normal type IV collagen). It also states that 'COL4A1 mutations segregate with porencephaly in human families', but the abstract names no specific human variants, families or carriers. The full text (Gould et al. 2005) is known to report human COL4A1 families, likely including a glycine substitution, but those details were not provided, so no variant records were created. A curator should review the full text and supplement for the human family variants and segregation data.

Abstract only. The reported variant (Lys325Asn) is in COL4A4, not COL4A1 or COL4A2. COL4A1/A2 were only mentioned as candidate genes that linkage analysis (13q33-q34) excluded in this Sardinian autosomal dominant Alport family. No COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual.

Comparative gene mapping study (mouse linkage mapping of human chromosome 13 homologs, including Col4a1 and Col4a2). No patients, no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants reported in individuals. Abstract only.

Only the title was available (no abstract). The title and PubTator hints suggest a functional mouse study of a Col4a2 mutation (G646D) affecting ryanodine receptor (RyR2) clustering and BK channel function in cerebral arteries. There is no indication of human patients carrying specific variants, so no variant records were created. The G646D mention comes only from automated entity hints and refers to a mouse model.

variants.phenotype_details: Title only: phenotype described as mimicking Sneddon's and Divry van Bogaert syndrome; no clinical details available.
evidence_quotes: Novel heterozygous COL4A2 variant c.2572A > G, p.(I858V) mimicking Sneddon's and Divry van Bogaert Syndrome.
variants.notes: Only the title was available; there was no abstract. The number of carriers, inheritance, phenotype specifics and transcript are unknown. One proband is assumed from the title-only case-report format. The Sneddon/Divry van Bogaert-like phenotype implies cerebrovascular and small-vessel involvement, but this was not stated, so phenotype_systems is left empty. This is a non-glycine missense variant.

extraction.extraction_notes: Title-only input with no abstract. A single variant, COL4A2 c.2572A>G p.(I858V), is named in the title, and the record is inferred from that. All counts are assumptions based on the likely case-report format, so the full text is needed to verify the number of carriers, inheritance, phenotype and classification.

variants.phenotype_details: Sporadic intracerebral hemorrhage in 4 US GOCHA/ERICH cases (2 lobar, 2 nonlobar); no association with age at onset, sex or ICH volume. Also found in 2 ICH-free Lothian Birth Cohort controls, one with self-reported hypertension and myocardial infarction. Absent from 1,078 US controls and 192 LINCHPIN ICH cases.
variants.functional_evidence: In silico only: molecular dynamics modelling predicted a 14.9-35.1% shortening of the triple-helical segment, and the stability calculator predicted a 2.2°C fall in Tm; no experimental work.
evidence_quotes: rs138269346COL4A1 was present in 4 ICH cases (2 lobar and 2 nonlobar ICH cases) and rs201716258COL4A2 was observed in another 2 ICH cases (1 lobar and 1 nonlobar ICH case).
Turning to the population-based LBC cohort, we identified 2 ICH-free controls who carry the minor allele of rs138269346COL4A1 but no carriers for rs201716258COL4A2.
One of these 2 ICH-free controls carrying the rs138269346COL4A1 in LBC self-reported a history of hypertension and myocardial infarction.

Rs138269346COL4A1 was deemed pathogenic due to its annotation across multiple prediction tools: moderate by SnpEff, deleterious by SIFT, probably damaging by PolyPhen, and probably damaging by LoFtool.
variants.notes: This is a rare-variant case-control study with nominal association testing (BinomiRare p=0.054 for nonlobar ICH); carriers were found by screening. n_tested=3514 is all study participants (2,133 US plus 1,381 Scottish); the 4 cases come from 1,055 US ICH cases. n_total_carriers=6 counts the 4 cases plus 2 ICH-free LBC controls. Further carriers in Geno2MP (5) and UK Biobank (1 proxy ICH case; 33 with vascular/heart problems) are database lookups and are not counted. The text says exon 5 but the figure transcription says exon 6. The Tm section writes 'I100T', apparently a typo. No c. notation or transcript is given. The variant is non-glycine, in the 7S domain.

variants.phenotype_details: Sporadic intracerebral hemorrhage in 2 US GOCHA/ERICH cases (1 lobar, 1 nonlobar) and 2 Scottish LINCHPIN cases. The LINCHPIN cases had nonlobar (lentiform) ICH at ages 85 and 73 (1 male, 1 female), a low small vessel disease score, and no history of ischemic stroke. Absent from US controls and from LBC controls.
variants.functional_evidence: In silico only: molecular dynamics modelling predicted a 15.7% shortening of the triple-helical segment, and the stability calculator predicted a 2.1-3.1°C rise in Tm; no experimental work.
evidence_quotes: rs138269346COL4A1 was present in 4 ICH cases (2 lobar and 2 nonlobar ICH cases) and rs201716258COL4A2 was observed in another 2 ICH cases (1 lobar and 1 nonlobar ICH case).
We detected 2 patients with ICH who carry the minor allele of rs201716258COL4A2 but no carriers for rs138269346COL4A1.
For rs201716258, both individuals developed nonlobar ICH in the right ventricle (ICH epicenter was lentiform) with a low small vessel disease score.
The ages of patients (1 male, 1 female) were 85 and 73 at the time of ICH, and there was no history of ischemic stroke.
variants.notes: This is a rare-variant case-control study; carriers were found by screening and association with ICH subtypes was nonsignificant (p>0.12). Pathogenicity predictions were mixed: SIFT tolerated, PolyPhen benign, CADD 4.7. The author text says His203Leu, but the figure transcription reads H203R; the author text is followed. The rsID is also printed as 'rs20176258' in one figure caption. Further carriers in Geno2MP (6) and UK Biobank (63 with vascular/heart problems) are not counted. No c. notation or transcript is given.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a targeted 13q34 sequencing case-control study: 1,055 ICH cases and 1,078 controls in the US, plus 192 LINCHPIN ICH cases and 1,189 LBC controls in Scotland. Only the 2 rare candidate variants that the authors highlight as found in ICH cases are extracted. The 39 annotated nonsynonymous variants (table e-2, Dryad) and the previously reported COL4A2 variants are not extracted, because they were not provided as individual-level data and/or were found in both cases and controls (association-type data). This is a review of the genetics of intracerebral hemorrhage. Only the title and abstract were provided, although the input was labelled full text. The abstract mentions rare and common variants in COL4A1 and COL4A2 in general terms. It reports no specific variants in specific individuals and no new patients, so no variant records were created.

This is a review of congenital anterior segment disorders. The text provided contains only the abstract and two summary tables. COL4A1 appears in those tables at gene level only: its ocular expression, autosomal dominant inheritance, missense and rare splice variants, and minor phenotypes (corneal opacity, Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly, microphthalmia, cataract) with low penetrance. No specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is reported in any specific individual. The body text beyond the tables was not provided.

Only the title was available; there is no abstract or full text. The title reports 'a novel, pathogenic COL4A1 missense variant' in a single neonate with thrombotic microangiopathic leukoencephalopathy. This is a small_vessel phenotype, and the paper calls it pathogenic. The specific variant is not named, and there is no information on inheritance, n_tested or other phenotypes. For that reason no VariantEvidence record was created. A curator should retrieve the full text to identify the variant (c./p. notation, transcript) and its inheritance. Paper type was inferred from the title as a single-patient case report.

Population-based paediatric polymicrogyria cohort (n=109 total; 90 genetically tested; 77 by GS/ES). The paper mentions one individual with presumed vascular aetiology of PMG who carried 'a pathogenic variant in COL4A1' and was therefore classified as genetic. COL4A1 also appears in Supplementary Table 1 under 'Pathogenic/probably pathogenic' single-gene variants, with no count given, so presumably n=1. No specific variant (no c./p. notation), no inheritance and no individual phenotype beyond presumed vascular-pattern PMG is reported. For that reason no VariantEvidence record was created. A curator may wish to note this unspecified COL4A1 pathogenic variant carrier: polymicrogyria with presumed prenatal vascular insult, denominator 90 genetically tested out of 109. Relevant quote: 'Furthermore, one additional individual with presumed vascular aetiology had a pathogenic variant in COL4A1 and therefore was classified as genetic.' The authors state that a follow-up paper on the genetic results is in preparation; that paper may give the specific variant.

Whole-exome sequencing of 387 Saudi ischemic stroke patients versus ~20,230 Saudi Human Genome Project controls, analysed by gene-burden testing (TRAPD) and a rare-variant polygenic risk score. COL4A1 and COL4A2 are reported only as aggregate gene-level burden counts: COL4A2 had 27 heterozygous and 1 homozygous case carriers (dominant-model p = 2.70E-07); COL4A1 had 13 heterozygous case carriers (p = 0.073). No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are named in specific individuals in the text provided, and no per-patient phenotypes are given. Supplementary Table S1, said to list the rare impactful variants used for the PRS, was not provided in the input; it may contain variant-level COL4A1/COL4A2 data and could be checked by a curator. The supplementary gene-burden table provided was filtered (6 of 181 rows kept). No variant records were created.

This paper describes a curated database (NCGR) of genes and variants compiled from previously published NESHIE and cerebral palsy studies; it reports no new patients. The only specific COL4A1 variant named in the text is NM_001845:c.2263G>A, in a patient with CP due to birth asphyxia. That patient is cited from an earlier publication (reference not resolvable in the provided text), so no record was created. The other COL4A1 variants are said to be catalogued in Supplementary Tables 1, 2 and 7, which were not provided; only Supplementary Table 6 (study details) and the GO enrichment data were included. No COL4A2 variants are mentioned. A COL4A4 variant (NM_000092.5:c.4720C>T) is also cited from prior work but is outside the scope of COL4A1/COL4A2.

Pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants were found only in PKD1, COL3A1, SMAD3, TGFB2, LOX, MYLK and YY1AP1. Whole-exome sequencing study of 21 patients (20 unrelated families; cases C01 and C09 are brothers) with corneal neuralgia after LASIK/PRK. The text reports low-frequency COL4A2 variants in 4 cases (C08, C09, C18 and C21), including a homozygous COL4A2 missense variant in C21. variants.phenotype_details: 41-year-old Caucasian male classified as NMD-ADPKD (no PKD1/PKD2 mutation); bilateral well-formed kidney cysts, minimally enlarged kidneys (height-adjusted TKV 284 and 294 ml/m at enrollment and 4-year follow-up), eGFR 77, CKD stage 2, class IB; imaging consistent with HANAC syndrome rather than ADPKD; genetic diagnosis HANAC-like syndrome. Family history not available.
evidence_quotes: 6 | NMD-ADPKDf | 41/M (Caucasian) | eGFR:77 (78)/ CKD stage 2 (2)/ class IB | Not available | COL4A1: exon31:c.C2351T: p. P784L | HANAC-like syndrome | Missense, likely pathogenic | 1 × 10–5 | Noneg

In the current study, we found a third NMD-ADPKD patient with a heterozygous COL4A1 missense mutation that results in a proline-to-lysine substitution that met criteria for being likely pathogenic (Table 1, patient 6; Supplementary Methods).

A review of imaging for this patient after the molecular finding of a COL4A1 mutation showed minimally enlarged kidneys with height-adjusted TKV of 284 and 294 ml/m at enrollment and 4-year follow-up, respectively, with fewer cysts and well-preserved normal-appearing intervening renal parenchyma consistent with those seen in HANAC syndrome rather than ADPKD (Figure 2e).
We performed WES on a total of 179 unrelated patients with bilateral kidney cysts and CKD.

Although labelled full text, the input contained only the title and abstract. The paper is a whole-exome sequencing study of 43 cervical artery dissection (CeAD) patients: 28 familial CeAD patients from 17 pedigrees and 15 recurrent CeAD patients. The abstract states that 5 of 17 familial pedigrees carried 'CeAD-causing' variants in a gene list that includes COL4A1. It does not name the specific COL4A1 variant, the carrier pedigree, any phenotype or the inheritance, so no variant record could be created. No COL4A2 variant is mentioned. The full text and supplementary tables are likely to contain the variant-level COL4A1 details and should be reviewed by a curator. Note that the authors' 'CeAD-causing' label rests on in-silico prediction (SIFT/PolyPhen-2) or ClinVar and gene-panel membership, not on ACMG classification.

extraction.extraction_notes: WES in 550 CAKUT families; 12 families with 10 distinct COL4A1 missense variants in 14 individuals (Table 1). All variants inherited from a parent (m=maternal, p=paternal) except two with segregation n/d; many are present in gnomAD at low het counts and parents presumably unaffected (incomplete penetrance not discussed in provided text). variants.phenotype_details: Carrier was a 3C-Dijon population-based participant (aged 65+) in the minimal-SVD extreme group, defined as lowest quartile of WMH burden and no MRI-defined brain infarcts. No gradient echo imaging was done, so microbleeds and haemorrhage were not assessed. No disease phenotype was reported.
evidence_quotes: We also observed two minimal-SVD participants carrying a heterozygote genotype at one glycine residue altering missense variant in COL4A1 [NM_001845.4 (COL4A1): c.3158G > A (p.Gly1053Asp), participant level depth coverage = 125× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99], and one nonsense (stop gained) variant in COL4A2 [NM_001846.2 (COL4A2) c.3766C > T (p.Arg1256Ter), participant level depth coverage = 77× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99].

Intriguingly we observed two missense variants in COL4A1 and COL4A2 in 3C-Dijon participants with minimal SVD, with typical characteristics of SVD causing mutations, although they have not been described previously in SVD families.
variants.notes: Incidental finding by WES screening of a 512-person extreme-SVD subsample; no family studied and no Sanger validation was described. The carrier had minimal SVD, which the authors suggest may reflect low penetrance. No inheritance data.

variants.phenotype_details: Carrier was a 3C-Dijon population-based participant (aged 65+) in the minimal-SVD extreme group, defined as lowest quartile of WMH burden and no brain infarcts. No disease phenotype was reported.
evidence_quotes: We also observed two minimal-SVD participants carrying a heterozygote genotype at one glycine residue altering missense variant in COL4A1 [NM_001845.4 (COL4A1): c.3158G > A (p.Gly1053Asp), participant level depth coverage = 125× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99], and one nonsense (stop gained) variant in COL4A2 [NM_001846.2 (COL4A2) c.3766C > T (p.Arg1256Ter), participant level depth coverage = 77× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99].

Heterozygous glycine residue changes and nonsense mutations in COL4A1 and COL4A2 are typically described in SVD families with cerebral bleedings, although, to our knowledge, these specific variants have not been described previously in any SVD family.
variants.notes: The Discussion inconsistently calls both variants 'missense', but the Results specify a stop-gained variant. It appears as '*6521R' (mirrored R1256*) in Supplementary Fig. 4. Found by WES screening; no family studied and no Sanger validation. No inheritance data.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a population-based extreme-phenotype WES association study (3C-Dijon, n=512 sequenced). The COL4A1/COL4A2 SNP rs2275842 in Table 2 is an association SNP and was not extracted. The COL4A2 GWAS intronic SNPs mentioned in the Discussion were also excluded. Supplementary Figs 3-4 list many COL4A1/COL4A2 protein-modifying rare variants, with mirrored or garbled labels. They indicate only case/control group membership, without individual-level detail or counts, so they were not extracted. The supplementary file was truncated: 6 of 32 sheets were not included, possibly Supplementary Table 5 with variant listings. Both extracted carriers belonged to the minimal-SVD (control) group, and neither had a reported affected phenotype.
